questions.question: When there's a power outage and phones and card readers can't be used, which form of money fits that situation?

options.text: Electronic money (because you can tap your phone to pay)
Crypto-assets (because you can exchange on the internet)
CBDC (because it's reliable since issued by the central bank)
Cash (because it can be used without electricity or internet)

answer.text: Cash (because it can be used without electricity or internet)

questions.question: In a country, the following four initiatives are being considered. Which is most directly connected to "financial inclusion"?

options.text: Renovating the large bank branches in urban areas to be nicer, raising customer satisfaction
Spreading mobile payment services so rural residents can transfer and pay with phones
Redesigning all bills to be harder to counterfeit
Strengthening services from urban banks for people who already have accounts

answer.text: Spreading mobile payment services so rural residents can transfer and pay with phones

questions.question: You changed the payment for koshary from cash to electronic money on your phone. Which correctly describes what "changes" and "doesn't change" with this switch?

options.text: Electronic money loses the "medium of exchange" function, so both form and function change
Cash and electronic money are both physical money, so the form doesn't change
The form changes, but none of money's three functions change
Cash doesn't have the "store of value" function, so only the function changes

answer.text: The form changes, but none of money's three functions change

questions.question: Crypto-assets fluctuate sharply in price, while CBDC is designed to be stable. What's the biggest reason for this difference?

options.text: Crypto-assets can only be used on the internet, but CBDC can be used in actual shops
Crypto-assets can only be owned by entrepreneurs, but CBDC can only be owned by limited countries
Crypto-assets are made with old technology, but CBDC is made with the latest technology
Crypto-assets have no central bank backing, but CBDC is issued and managed by the central bank

answer.text: Crypto-assets have no central bank backing, but CBDC is issued and managed by the central bank

questions.question: Which correctly describes money's "form" and "function"?

options.text: Even as money's form changes, the three functions are common, but strengths and weaknesses differ by form
Even as money's form changes, functions don't change, and no form has weaknesses—all are equally usable
When money's form changes, the three functions—"unit of account," "medium of exchange," and "store of value"—also change
Money's form doesn't change with the times—the same form has been used from the shell era to today

answer.text: Even as money's form changes, the three functions are common, but strengths and weaknesses differ by form

questions.question: The money you deposited at the bank was used as financing for the cafe owner. The depositor doesn't know the owner. In this case, how did the depositor's money reach them?

options.text: The depositor found the cafe owner themselves and handed money directly
The bank pooled the depositor's money and lent part of it to the owner
The government collected the depositor's money as taxes and delivered it to the owner
The cafe owner directly accessed the depositor's bank account and withdrew the money

answer.text: The bank pooled the depositor's money and lent part of it to the owner

questions.question: Which of the following counts as "direct finance"?

options.text: You ask family "I'm short on money this month, lend me some" and borrow directly
Money you deposit at a bank is pooled by the bank and used as financing to companies
A company issues stocks or bonds and gathers money directly from investors without going through a bank
You borrow a game software from a friend, play it, and later exchange with your own software

answer.text: A company issues stocks or bonds and gathers money directly from investors without going through a bank

questions.question: What's the name of the system where people broadly call for funds from the general public via the internet, gathering money for new ideas or businesses?

options.text: Crowdfunding
Indirect finance
Direct finance
Inflation

answer.text: Crowdfunding

questions.question: Suppose you're planning to open a small new shop with a new idea in the future. When gathering funds, which is the most reasonable approach?

options.text: Depending on the scale and stage of the business, compare multiple gathering methods and use the one that fits
Issuing stock can gather large amounts at once, so it's most advantageous to choose stock from the very start
Going through a bank is the safest, so use only indirect finance to gather money at any stage
Banks and investors have complex systems, so open the shop using only your own savings without relying on anyone

answer.text: Depending on the scale and stage of the business, compare multiple gathering methods and use the one that fits

questions.question: If in finance's bridging system, no compensation (cost) arose when money or goods were made available, what do you think would happen?

options.text: Banks would do financing using only their own funds, and there'd be no need to gather money from depositors
Money providers would become even more active, and the bridging system would work more vigorously
Only borrowers would keep benefiting, and the gap between providers and borrowers would widen
Money providers would have no return, no one would provide money, and the bridging system would stop

answer.text: Money providers would have no return, no one would provide money, and the bridging system would stop

lessons.lesson: Types and Roles of Financial Institutions

questions.question: Commercial banks (ordinary banks) take our deposits and lend money to companies and individuals. So what role do you think a central bank has?

options.text: A bank that takes deposits from the general public and delivers higher returns than commercial banks
A bank that issues the country's money (currency), supports commercial banks, and keeps the currency's value stable
A bank that lends money to people short on money at a lower compensation than commercial banks
A bank that specializes in foreign currency for buying imported goods from abroad

answer.text: A bank that issues the country's money (currency), supports commercial banks, and keeps the currency's value stable

questions.question: The central bank has three roles: "bank of issuance," "bank of banks," and "bank of the government." If the central bank with these three roles didn't exist, what problems do you think would happen in society?

options.text: Issuing paper money and supporting banks would become impossible, and trust in money couldn't be maintained across society
Commercial banks would each issue their own paper money, becoming a more convenient system
The government would directly manage all deposits and financing, replacing commercial banks
Commercial banks would help each other out, so no major problems would happen

answer.text: Issuing paper money and supporting banks would become impossible, and trust in money couldn't be maintained across society

questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the roles of "commercial bank," "securities company," and "insurance company"?

options.text: Commercial bank = takes deposits and lends to companies, securities company = collects premiums, prepares for risk, and invests money, insurance company = brokers stocks and bonds
Commercial bank = brokers stocks and bonds, securities company = collects premiums, prepares for risk, and invests money, insurance company = takes deposits and lends to companies
Commercial bank = collects premiums, prepares for risk, and invests money, securities company = takes deposits and lends to companies, insurance company = brokers stocks and bonds
Commercial bank = takes deposits and lends to companies, securities company = brokers stocks and bonds, insurance company = collects premiums, prepares for risk, and invests the money

answer.text: Commercial bank = takes deposits and lends to companies, securities company = brokers stocks and bonds, insurance company = collects premiums, prepares for risk, and invests the money

questions.question: If a system like microfinance didn't exist, what impact do you think there would be on society?

options.text: People who can't borrow from banks couldn't get money, and there would be people unable to start businesses
Even big companies couldn't borrow money, and all economic activity in society would stop
Ordinary banks would start providing small loans in place of microfinance, so there would be no impact
People can start businesses without borrowing money, so even without microfinance, no problem

answer.text: People who can't borrow from banks couldn't get money, and there would be people unable to start businesses

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.text: Commercial banks are financial institutions that take deposits from us and lend that money to companies and individuals
Central banks are special banks that issue currency, support commercial banks, and manage the government's money
Securities companies are financial institutions that take our deposits and lend to companies, with the same role as commercial banks
Microfinance is a system that delivers small amounts of money to people who can't borrow from banks

answer.text: Securities companies are financial institutions that take our deposits and lend to companies, with the same role as commercial banks

questions.question: A large factory in a town was closed due to business troubles, and 200 employees lost their jobs. What impact do you think this event has on shops near the factory?

options.text: Even with the factory closed, there's no major impact on nearby shop sales
If the factory disappears, new shops will be built where it was, so the economy improves
With 200 fewer people's shopping, sales at nearby shops are likely to fall
Even if employees lose jobs, they live off savings, so consumption nearby doesn't change

answer.text: With 200 fewer people's shopping, sales at nearby shops are likely to fall

questions.question: The mayor of a certain city announced "this year, we'll significantly cut the road maintenance budget and put that money into the city's savings." Suppose a shop owner in the city is worried. Which of the following is the most appropriate reason?

options.text: Road maintenance doesn't affect product delivery, so no need to worry
Damaged roads delay deliveries and make it harder for customers to come, affecting sales
Putting the road budget into savings stabilizes city finances, which is good for shops too
Road maintenance relates to citizens' lives but doesn't directly relate to shop management

answer.text: Damaged roads delay deliveries and make it harder for customers to come, affecting sales

questions.question: In a country's economic news, it was reported "three major banks have fallen into management difficulty and have nearly halted new financing to companies." If this situation continues, what impact do you think will spread through that country's society?

options.text: Even if banks stop financing, companies can secure funds on their own, so impact is limited
Even if financing stops, consumer shopping doesn't change, so no impact on the economy as a whole
Banks stopping financing means companies avoid wasteful debt, stabilizing their management
New businesses won't start, employment and consumption decrease, and the virtuous cycle reverses

answer.text: New businesses won't start, employment and consumption decrease, and the virtuous cycle reverses

questions.question: Suppose you're thinking about "ways to deliver financial services to people living in areas without nearby bank branches." Based on what you've learned, which is most promising?

options.text: Spreading services using new technology like smartphone payments and transfers
Building many new bank branches in rural areas to physically deliver traditional counters to all regions
Concentrating financial services on urban residents and having rural people continue cash-based lives
New technology lacks reliability, so handle it only within the framework of traditional bank financing

answer.text: Spreading services using new technology like smartphone payments and transfers

questions.question: In a gameia group, a member who received the lump sum third stopped payments from the 4th month. What impact is there on the remaining members?

options.text: Gameia has built-in insurance, so the amount from the person who quit is automatically covered
The amount gathered each month falls short, and members later in the order receive less
The central bank supervises gameia, so collection is forced from the person who quit
The amount from the person who quit isn't counted from the start, so no impact on others

answer.text: The amount gathered each month falls short, and members later in the order receive less

questions.question: In a rural village in Egypt, there's no bank branch, and residents can't receive financing. Someone in this village wants to open a bakery. What's a possible means of preparing startup funds?

options.text: Contact the central bank directly and ask for a special loan
Issue stocks and gather funds from investors worldwide to open in the village
Opening a business is impossible in areas without banks, so give up
Form a gameia with village friends and receive lump sums in turn

answer.text: Form a gameia with village friends and receive lump sums in turn

questions.question: The popularity of a sneaker has risen and the price has gone up. At this time, what do you think the sneaker maker would do?

options.text: Since the price got too high, they reduce the quantity and lower the price
They stop making sneakers and start making completely different products
Regardless of price, they keep making the same amount as before
If they can sell at a high price, they'll try to make and sell more

answer.text: If they can sell at a high price, they'll try to make and sell more

questions.question: A popular game software was released. Right after release, supply was tight, and online it was being sold at higher than retail price. But when the maker increased production, the price came down. Which correctly describes this situation?

options.text: Game demand suddenly dropped, so the price went down without restricting supply
Supply increased and caught up with demand, so the price approached equilibrium and went down
The shop restricted supply by their own judgment, so the price moved downward
Demand and supply were originally at equilibrium, so they naturally went down over time

answer.text: Supply increased and caught up with demand, so the price approached equilibrium and went down

questions.question: Among the following scenes, which had a price rise caused by a "supply-side change"?

options.text: Sneaker prices rose because a famous athlete using them became a hot topic
Hotel room prices rose because more people traveled during summer vacation
Vegetable prices rose more than usual because heavy rain damaged crops
Notebook prices rose because more people bought stationery as the new school year started

answer.text: Vegetable prices rose more than usual because heavy rain damaged crops

questions.question: Which of the following is "closest to a monopoly market"?

options.text: There are many bakeries near the school, all competing on price and deliciousness
Only one company provides water in a region, and residents have to use that company
Many shoe shops exist online, and people can choose by price and design
Several hamburger shops are in the neighborhood, trying to differentiate by taste and menu

answer.text: Only one company provides water in a region, and residents have to use that company

questions.question: In winter, a major cold wave came and gas prices for heating rose sharply. However, the number of people using gas barely decreased. Which correctly describes this situation?

options.text: The cold wave made supply unable to keep up, so prices rose. People kept using gas because it's necessary for daily life
Gas supply increased, raising prices. The number of users didn't decrease because the price was originally low
Gas is a monopoly market with high prices, and users didn't decrease because gas is highly popular
Gas has large price elasticity, so even with price rises, the number of users barely changed

answer.text: The cold wave made supply unable to keep up, so prices rose. People kept using gas because it's necessary for daily life

questions.question: Which of the following news items is about "CPI"?

options.text: Egypt's GDP this year grew 3% over last year
"Prices of daily life products rose 7% over last year"
"Last month, factory production volume increased significantly by 10%"
"This year, 10 new factories opened"

answer.text: "Prices of daily life products rose 7% over last year"

questions.question: When you want to know whether inflation is happening, what do you think you should look at?

options.text: Look at GDP and check whether the amount of goods and services produced in the country increased
Check whether the price of one product you often buy has gone up
Track the prices of many daily life products together and check whether they've risen overall
Count the number of factories in the country and check whether places of production increased

answer.text: Track the prices of many daily life products together and check whether they've risen overall

questions.question: In a country, many new factories and companies started appearing, and job openings increased. What do you think happens to this country's unemployment rate?

options.text: With more factories and companies and more workplaces, unemployment rate falls
Even with more factories, mechanization advances so labor isn't needed much, and unemployment rate doesn't change much
When job openings increase, even more people who want to work appear, so unemployment rate rises
Factory increases cause competition and some companies that can't keep up appear, so unemployment rate rises

answer.text: With more factories and companies and more workplaces, unemployment rate falls

questions.question: Egypt's income from the "Suez Canal" falls under which of the following?

options.text: Income earned by Egypt exporting goods to foreign countries, included in trade balance
Sales of products made within Egypt, included in GDP
Income from providing canal transit services to foreign ships, included in current account balance
Money sent by Egyptians working abroad to family, included in current account balance

answer.text: Income from providing canal transit services to foreign ships, included in current account balance

questions.question: For a country, these numbers were announced: "Economic growth rate is positive (economy growing)," "Inflation rate is mild (prices stable)," "Unemployment rate is high (jobs hard to find)." Which correctly reads this country's economy?

options.text: The economy is not growing, prices are rising sharply—a dangerous state
The economy is shrinking, prices haven't risen much—a stable state
The economy is growing, prices are stable, jobs are plentiful—an ideal state
The economy is growing, but the rate of people who can't find work despite searching is high

answer.text: The economy is growing, but the rate of people who can't find work despite searching is high

questions.question: The Suez Canal incident where ships got stuck connects to your sneakers not arriving. Why do you think that's happening?

options.text: The sneakers might have been carried on a ship passing through the Suez Canal
The Suez Canal isn't related to sneaker production, so the delay is for a different reason
The Suez Canal problem stopped Egypt's economy, and shops can't operate
Suez Canal transit fees dropped, and fewer people are buying sneakers

answer.text: The sneakers might have been carried on a ship passing through the Suez Canal

questions.question: When starting your own desired business, which of the following four countries would let you start and run a business most freely?

options.text: A country where anyone can open a shop, but the products you can sell are chosen from a list set by the country, and prices must be within ranges set by the country
A country where anyone can open a shop, and you decide what to sell at what price by watching surrounding shops and customers
A country where once a year, the country assigns each shop's production limit, and within that amount you can make and sell any product
A country where anyone can open a shop, but prices are decided in common across all shops by industry groups, and keeping that price is a condition

answer.text: A country where anyone can open a shop, and you decide what to sell at what price by watching surrounding shops and customers

questions.question: When economic conditions or prices worsen, by which means can the central bank (CBE) respond?

options.text: Increase public works like building roads and schools to create workplaces
Distribute money directly to all unemployed people to quickly increase consumption
Place new taxes on imports from abroad to raise imported product prices
Adjust the amount of money circulating in the market to make money flow easier

answer.text: Adjust the amount of money circulating in the market to make money flow easier

questions.question: In a country, the unemployment rate has sharply risen, and at the same time, the inflation rate is also rising. How do you think the government and central bank each act?

options.text: The government increases public works, and the central bank increases the amount of money in the market
The government increases public works, and the central bank tightens the amount of money in the market
The government decreases public works, and the central bank increases the amount of money in the market
The central bank increases public works, and the government tightens the amount of money in the market

answer.text: The government increases public works, and the central bank tightens the amount of money in the market

questions.question: Due to global logistics disruption, Suez Canal traffic decreased, and Egypt's imported goods prices rose. As a result, CPI sharply rose and domestic consumption is starting to decline. Which of the following best explains this situation?

options.text: Since domestic CPI rose due to logistics disruption, the government needs to respond with fiscal policy
Since domestic CPI rose due to logistics disruption, CBE needs to respond with fiscal policy
Since domestic CPI rose due to logistics disruption, CBE needs to respond with monetary policy
Although domestic CPI rose due to logistics disruption, neither government nor CBE needs to respond

answer.text: Since domestic CPI rose due to logistics disruption, CBE needs to respond with monetary policy

questions.question: Suppose there's a society with a rule that "people whose wealth exceeds a certain standard pay a fixed amount to society every year based on calculation. This is defined as an obligation." Which of the following is the most fundamental feature of this system?

options.text: It spreads through society because many people participate voluntarily
The payment amount can be decided freely by the payer each time
It is a system socially recognized when only those who want to pay do so
If conditions are met, there is a duty to pay, and refusing is not allowed

answer.text: If conditions are met, there is a duty to pay, and refusing is not allowed

questions.question: Among the following four people, who do you think is subject to the obligation to pay Zakat?

options.text: A Muslim with almost no savings, barely getting by in daily life
A Muslim who stably holds wealth exceeding the Nisab threshold
A person who previously exceeded Nisab but is now below the threshold
A person with sufficient wealth but who isn't Muslim

answer.text: A Muslim who stably holds wealth exceeding the Nisab threshold

questions.question: Among the following four scenarios, which best describes Zakat? (1) Pay once a year because wealth exceeded the threshold (2) Give whenever you feel like it, in any amount (3) Give a calculated amount to people fitting the defined categories (4) Give to anyone, anytime, freely
Which of the following best describes a social effect of Zakat?

options.text: By paying Zakat, the payer's own wealth becomes easier to grow in the future
Money flows from people with wealth to society as a whole, narrowing inequality
The more Zakat one pays, the higher one's social credibility becomes
Zakat is a religious ritual, so it has no direct effect on society or the economy

answer.text: Money flows from people with wealth to society as a whole, narrowing inequality

questions.question: Which of the following best describes Zakat?

options.text: Any Muslim with wealth must pay it every year without fail
It is a voluntary religious act done only by those who want to pay
A Muslim who has wealth exceeding Nisab has the obligation to pay
Zakat and Sadaqa are the same; both are obligatory forms of giving

answer.text: A Muslim who has wealth exceeding Nisab has the obligation to pay

questions.question: For the Zakat obligation to apply to someone holding wealth that exceeds Nisab, one more condition must be met. Which do you think it is?

options.text: They have been continuously engaged in a specific profession or job for a necessary period
They have obtained agreement from all family members and registered together
They have continuously held wealth exceeding Nisab for one year
They exceed Nisab only for a certain fixed period each year

answer.text: They have continuously held wealth exceeding Nisab for one year

questions.question: How much Zakat does someone who continuously held wealth of 580,000 EGP, exceeding Nisab, for one year pay?

Among the following people (1) to (4), who is included as a Zakat recipient? Choose the correct combination. [People list] (1) Someone who had their money stolen while traveling and is having trouble getting home (2) Someone with sufficient income who can save stably every month (3) Someone who can't pay their debt and is struggling with daily life (4) Someone whose wealth exceeds Nisab and is on the side paying Zakat
Which of the following best describes the Zakat system?

options.text: It is a system where the country legally and forcibly collects, like taxes
It is a system without a delivery mechanism, where one must always deliver directly oneself
It is a type of tax, and not paying leads to legal punishment
It is a system where individuals pay it as an obligation, separate from the country's management

answer.text: It is a system where individuals pay it as an obligation, separate from the country's management

questions.question: We learned that there are two types of Zakat: "Wealth Zakat" and "Fitr Zakat." Which of the following best describes these?

options.text: Wealth Zakat is a conditional obligation; Fitr Zakat is basically paid with food
Both Wealth Zakat and Fitr Zakat are systems of the same nature
Wealth Zakat is basically paid with food; Fitr Zakat is calculated at 2.5%
Both Wealth Zakat and Fitr Zakat are paid by calculating at 2.5%

answer.text: Wealth Zakat is a conditional obligation; Fitr Zakat is basically paid with food

questions.question: Someone who received Zakat money used it to buy groceries. After this, how do you think the money paid to the shop moves through society?

options.text: It stops with the receiver and isn't used, so it doesn't pass to anyone
It becomes the shop's income, then passes to another person and flows through society
The amount the receiver used disappears from society and can't be used anymore
It's used only within the receiver's family as pocket money

answer.text: It becomes the shop's income, then passes to another person and flows through society

questions.question: Among the following viewpoints, which differ between Zakat and taxes? Choose the correct combination. [Viewpoint list] (1) The function of letting money flow to society and narrowing inequality (2) Who has to pay (3) Where the collected money goes (4) The role of contributing to social stability
Among the following four, which is closest to the action forbidden as "Riba" in Islamic finance?

options.text: Two people pool money together and share both profits and losses
A bank buys a product instead and sells it at an added price in installments
Lending a book to a friend and receiving the same book back after reading
Lending money and receiving more back regardless of the outcome

answer.text: Lending money and receiving more back regardless of the outcome

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why the Murabaha system doesn't fall under "Riba"?

options.text: It's a form where the bank buys and sells goods, not money lending
The bank provides the product for free, so there's no money exchange
Only credit moves, not money, so no wealth transfer occurs
The bank receives no profit and doesn't add markup or use installments

answer.text: It's a form where the bank buys and sells goods, not money lending

questions.question: Which of the following combinations identifies the statements (1-4) that do NOT apply as basic principles of Islamic finance? [Idea list] (1) Avoid methods of lending money and receiving more back regardless of outcome (2) Completely forbid all financial systems and do no money exchanges at all (3) Use alternative methods like Murabaha and Sukuk that avoid Riba (4) Money providers bear no risk; only borrowers bear losses
Which of the following counts as a "public enterprise"?

options.text: A local grocery store run by a family of three
A restaurant operated by a major corporation
A bus the city operates for local transportation
A variety store chain operated with foreign capital

answer.text: A bus the city operates for local transportation

questions.question: Among the following scenes, which applies to a "sole proprietorship"?

options.text: A local eatery run by a family of three who formed a company
A clothing shop started by several friends who invested and founded a company
A workshop a craftsperson started alone and runs by themselves
A famous nationwide cafe chain operated by a major corporation

answer.text: A workshop a craftsperson started alone and runs by themselves

questions.question: Among the following scenes, which applies to "unlimited liability"?

options.text: A stock company's shareholder bears liability only for the money they invested
A general partnership company's members take on all the company's debt themselves
A limited liability company's members bear liability only within the money they invested
A public enterprise's operating body runs the business using the national or city budget

answer.text: A general partnership company's members take on all the company's debt themselves

questions.question: Suppose Ren wants to start a cafe using local ingredients together with family and a few acquaintances. He wants to make a profit and share it among everyone, supporting each other with a small group and continuing for a long time. Which form is most suitable for Ren?

options.text: Stock company (a form that issues stock to gather funds from many people)
Limited liability company (a form where a small number of members all run it with limited liability)
Limited partnership company (a form run by unlimited liability members and limited liability members)
NPO (a form that doesn't distribute income but uses it for activities for society)

answer.text: Limited liability company (a form where a small number of members all run it with limited liability)

questions.question: Someone wants to create a place for learning support where children in their area can study with peace of mind. Rather than making a profit, they want to continue the activity for a long time and deliver support to as many children as possible for free. Which form is most suitable for this person to choose?

options.text: Stock company (a form that distributes business profit to shareholders)
Sole proprietorship (a form where one runs the business as an individual)
NPO (a form that doesn't distribute income and acts for society)
Public enterprise (a form operated by the national or local government)

answer.text: NPO (a form that doesn't distribute income and acts for society)

questions.question: Looking at one company's money movement over a year, the money that came into the company was 12,000,000 EGP, the money used to run the business was 9,000,000 EGP, and the money left in hand was 3,000,000 EGP. Which of the following words best represents this "3,000,000 EGP left in hand"?

options.text: Revenue
Expenses
Corporate profit
Stock

answer.text: Corporate profit

questions.question:
A company's management is discussing how to use this year's corporate profit:
"This year we have no plans to build a new factory, and new product development has just wrapped up. The shareholders' share has already been decided separately. Let's keep the remaining corporate profit inside the company as a reserve for whatever may come in the years ahead."
Which of the four does this use of the remaining corporate profit correspond to?

options.text: Dividend
Retained earnings
Capital investment
Research and development

answer.text: Retained earnings

questions.question: A large stock company has 10,000 shareholders. In this company, who actually makes the decisions about daily management?

options.text: All 10,000 shareholders gather and discuss almost every day to decide
The single shareholder who invested the most money decides alone
The directors chosen at the shareholders' meeting discuss and decide at the board of directors
All the employees working at the company gather and decide by majority vote

answer.text: The directors chosen at the shareholders' meeting discuss and decide at the board of directors

questions.question:
Consider the following six people about a certain company. Which of the following is the most appropriate combination of people who count as that company's stakeholders?
① A person investing money in the company
② An employee working at the company
③ A customer buying the company's products
④ Another company from which the company purchases parts
⑤ A person living right near the company's factory
⑥ A person in another area who just happened to see the company mentioned on SNS, has never bought a product

options.text: The 3 people ①, ②, ③
The 4 people ①, ②, ③, ④
The 5 people ①, ②, ③, ④, ⑤
All 6 people ①, ②, ③, ④, ⑤, ⑥

answer.text: The 5 people ①, ②, ③, ④, ⑤

questions.question: In light of the four topics learned so far (corporate profit, uses of corporate profit, separation of ownership and management, stakeholders), choose the one description among the following four that is "incorrect."

options.text: A company's corporate profit is the money left in hand after subtracting expenses from revenue
A company divides corporate profit into capital investment/research and development, dividends, retained earnings, and so on
In a large stock company, the shareholders themselves directly decide and run all daily management
A company's stakeholders include the five parties: shareholders, employees, customers, business partners, and local community

answer.text: In a large stock company, the shareholders themselves directly decide and run all daily management

questions.question: Which best explains a company's "CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility)"?

options.text: An approach where a company aims only to maximize as much profit as possible and pours all its energy into pursuing corporate profit
An approach where a company takes responsibility only to the shareholders who provided money and focuses on making a profit to return a share to shareholders
An approach that refers only to activities where a company donates part of its earnings to the region or society, evaluated by the size of the donation amount

An approach where a company tries to fulfill three responsibilities—"following rules," "consideration for the environment," "contribution to society and the local area"—toward a wide range of parties such as shareholders and employees

answer.text: An approach where a company tries to fulfill three responsibilities—"following rules," "consideration for the environment," "contribution to society and the local area"—toward a wide range of parties such as shareholders and employees

questions.question:
Which of the following combinations (①-⑥) correctly identifies all actions related to compliance (conducting business while following laws and rules)?
① A food company makes products while properly following established safety standards
② A food company falsifies the labeling of product ingredients to differ from reality
③ A factory releases wastewater straight into the river without the legally required treatment
④ A company donates to support a local festival
⑤ A company divides its earnings as dividends to shareholders
⑥ A company manages working hours so employees' hours stay within the legal range

options.text: ① and ⑥
② and ③
①, ②, ③, ⑥
All of ① through ⑥

answer.text: ①, ②, ③, ⑥

questions.question:
An ice cream company has begun various efforts to keep running its business going forward. Among the following ① to ⑥, which combination includes all the actions that apply to "consideration for the environment"?
① Switched the electricity used at the factory to natural energy such as solar power
② Changed the containers holding products to easily recyclable paper material
③ Devised ways to make products easier for customers to buy by reviewing prices
④ Reduced waste from the factory and started using material that would have been thrown away in other products
⑤ Thoroughly observed the factory's safety standards as required by law
⑥ Aired the new product's commercial on many TV programs to raise its name recognition

options.text: ① and ④
①, ②, ④
①, ②, ④, ⑤
All of ① through ⑥

answer.text: ①, ②, ④

questions.question:
A food company is carrying out various efforts while continuing its business going forward. Among the following ① to ⑥, which combination includes all the actions that apply to a company's "contribution to society and the local area"?
① Sponsored a local children's soccer tournament and supported its operating costs
② Started an effort to recycle leftover materials from product-making into other products
③ The whole company supports employees volunteering for read-aloud sessions at the local library
④ Properly observes product safety standards as required by law
⑤ The whole company carried out activities sending products and donations to areas damaged by disaster
⑥ Greatly increased the budget for TV commercials to convey the appeal of new products

options.text: ① and ⑤
①, ③, ⑤
①, ③, ⑤, ⑥
①, ②, ③, ④, ⑤

answer.text: ①, ③, ⑤

questions.question:
An investor who provides money to companies evaluates them by the three axes of ESG. Among the following ① to ⑥, which combination includes all the efforts that apply to any of the three axes of ESG (E = Environment / S = Social / G = Governance)?
① Switched the electricity used at the factory to natural energy such as solar power
② Lowered product prices so that as many customers as possible can buy
③ Arranged an environment where employees can work safely and built good relationships with local people
④ Set up a mechanism to check company management and devised ways to prevent wrongdoing
⑤ Greatly reduced waste from the factory and set up a recycling mechanism too
⑥ Continues activities sending products and donations for local disaster recovery

options.text: ① and ⑤
①, ③, ④, ⑤, ⑥
①, ③, ④
All of ① through ⑥

answer.text: ①, ③, ④, ⑤, ⑥

questions.question: A food company announced an effort: "We switched all the electricity used at our factory to energy made by natural forces such as solar and wind power." Among the topics learned so far, which idea does this effort best apply to?

options.text: As compliance, properly following established laws and rules
As part of CSR, actually practicing consideration for the environment
Through the ESG investing mechanism, providing money to support other companies
Carrying out an activity to distribute the corporate profit the company gained as dividends to shareholders

answer.text: As part of CSR, actually practicing consideration for the environment

questions.question: After the phone bill paid from your household reaches the telecom company, how do you think it moves within society?

options.text: Only one manager within the company receives it, and it stays only in that person's hands
It divides among the company's workers, suppliers, the nation, and so on, and keeps moving beyond that
It never leaves the company even once, all saved up only for future business
It passes from the telecom company just once to another company, and the movement stops there

answer.text: It divides among the company's workers, suppliers, the nation, and so on, and keeps moving beyond that

questions.question: Which of the following best describes "economic circulation"?

options.text: A structure that holds together with only money exchanged between the two parties of households and companies
A structure where money, goods, services, and labor move among the three parties of households, companies, and government
A structure where the government is the center of activity, handing money one-directionally to households and companies
A structure where companies are the center of activity, handing money one-directionally to households and the government

answer.text: A structure where money, goods, services, and labor move among the three parties of households, companies, and government

questions.question: Which of the following best describes The Three Approaches to Measuring GDP?

options.text: The "making side," "receiving side," and "using side" are separate movements, but the totals happen to coincide
The "making side," "receiving side," and "using side" are separate movements, adjusted to become the same by a social rule
The "making side," "receiving side," and "using side" are the same movement seen from different standpoints, so the totals coincide
Only the "making side" is the correct figure, and the "receiving side" and "using side" move to match it

answer.text: The "making side," "receiving side," and "using side" are the same movement seen from different standpoints, so the totals coincide

questions.question: Suppose your household made a 1,000 EGP purchase. The shop uses 800 EGP of it for clerk salaries and stock, and keeps the rest inside the shop. The clerk who received salary also uses 640 EGP of it at another shop, and beyond that, similarly only a part is passed to the next. Which of the following best describes this phenomenon?

options.text: Adding up all the money used at each step of stocking and shopping, it becomes a far smaller amount than your household first paid
Adding up all the money used at each step of stocking and shopping, it becomes an infinitely larger amount than your household first paid
Adding up all the money used at each step of stocking and shopping, it becomes exactly the same amount as your household first paid
Adding up all the money used at each step of stocking and shopping, it becomes a far larger amount than your household first paid

answer.text: Adding up all the money used at each step of stocking and shopping, it becomes a far larger amount than your household first paid

questions.question: A friend said, "Even if you shop at a store, that's just for that store's sake and has nothing to do with society as a whole." Based on the ideas learned today, which of the following is the most appropriate response to the friend?

options.text: The money paid when shopping doesn't stop at the store; it divides into the clerks' salaries, suppliers, and the nation's taxes, and chains and moves further beyond that
The money paid when shopping passes to the store's clerks and suppliers, but the impact doesn't spread further, so the impact on society as a whole is limited
Even if the money paid when shopping is passed one after another through society, the overall total amount doesn't change, so the impact on society is the same as at first
The money paid when shopping gathers to the government as taxes and returns to society from there as public services, so it only has an impact through the government

answer.text: The money paid when shopping doesn't stop at the store; it divides into the clerks' salaries, suppliers, and the nation's taxes, and chains and moves further beyond that

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct order in which a T-shirt reaches the consumer's hands?

options.text: Cotton farmer → thread factory → sewing factory → fabric factory → logistics → shop → consumer
Cotton farmer → fabric factory → thread factory → sewing factory → shop → logistics → consumer
Thread factory → cotton farmer → fabric factory → sewing factory → logistics → shop → consumer
Cotton farmer → thread factory → fabric factory → sewing factory → logistics → shop → consumer

answer.text: Cotton farmer → thread factory → fabric factory → sewing factory → logistics → shop → consumer

questions.question: A thread factory bought cotton for 80 EGP, made it into thread, and sold it to a fabric factory for 200 EGP. Furthermore, the fabric factory bought that thread for 200 EGP, made it into fabric, and sold it to a sewing factory for 320 EGP. What is the total value added at the thread factory and the fabric factory respectively?

options.text: 120 EGP
200 EGP
240 EGP
320 EGP

answer.text: 240 EGP

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the "international division of labor"?

options.text: A mechanism where each country specializes in what it's good at and what's cost-effective, building up one product
A mechanism where only powerful countries make products, and other countries end up buying products from those countries
A mechanism aiming for countries to make the same product as each other and raise quality through competition
A mechanism where you create a company that does all stages within the country and deliberately avoid dealing with overseas companies

answer.text: A mechanism where each country specializes in what it's good at and what's cost-effective, building up one product

questions.question:
Which does each of these two correspond to, "international division of labor" or "outsourcing"?
① An Egyptian T-shirt brand company leaves the sewing to a factory in Vietnam where labor costs are low.
② An Egyptian apparel company leaves the operation of its own website to a specialist company strong in IT within Egypt.

options.text: Both ① and ② are international division of labor
① is international division of labor, ② is outsourcing
Both ① and ② are outsourcing
① is outsourcing, ② is international division of labor

answer.text: ① is international division of labor, ② is outsourcing

questions.question: One day a disaster occurred in the country where a fabric factory is located, and the fabric factory temporarily stopped. At this time, which of the following best describes what happens to the T-shirt's supply chain?

options.text: When the fabric factory stops, the impact spreads to the sewing factory, logistics, and shop beyond it, and ultimately T-shirts stop reaching the shop
Even if the fabric factory stops, a sewing factory in another country makes the fabric instead, so there's almost no impact on the flow to the shop
Even if the fabric factory stops, the thread factory and farmer keep moving as before, so the flow to the shop proceeds without particularly stalling
When the fabric factory stops, only that stage is delayed, but the later sewing factory and logistics stages keep moving as usual

answer.text: When the fabric factory stops, the impact spreads to the sewing factory, logistics, and shop beyond it, and ultimately T-shirts stop reaching the shop

questions.question: Which of the following best describes corporate tax?

options.text: A tax where, as soon as revenue comes in, part of it is paid to the government
A tax where part of the final corporate profit a company produced is paid to the government
A tax where the people working at a company pay part of their salary to the government
A tax where part of the expenses a company uses for business is paid to the government

answer.text: A tax where part of the final corporate profit a company produced is paid to the government

questions.question:
Among the following life scenes, which combination correctly identifies those that use a "public service"? ① Walking the road of the school route to go to school
② Buying snacks at a convenience store
③ Drinking water from the home's water supply
④ Buying and drinking coffee at a cafe
⑤ Calling 119 to call an ambulance
⑥ Paying a fee to a video streaming service to watch a movie

options.text: ①③⑤
①②④
②④⑥
③⑤⑥

answer.text: ①③⑤

questions.question: Which of the following best explains the main reason the government sets up mechanisms of regulation and licensing for companies?

options.text: To let companies advance their business more freely, unbound by rules
To let the government gather more taxes from companies
To set rules necessary for company activities so everyone in society can live with peace of mind
To give business preferential treatment only to certain limited companies

answer.text: To set rules necessary for company activities so everyone in society can live with peace of mind

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a special economic zone?

options.text: A special place decided so that only people of a certain country can live in that area
An area designated by the government where taxes are set higher than other places
A special area where the government gives preferential treatment on taxes and rules to bring in companies
An area created exclusively for factories and businesses the government directly runs

answer.text: A special area where the government gives preferential treatment on taxes and rules to bring in companies

questions.question: Which is incorrect about the relationship between companies and government?

options.text: A company is set up to pay part of the final corporate profit it produced to the government as corporate tax
A company also conducts its business activities while using public services like roads, police, electricity, and water supply
Regulation and licensing are rules the government decides so everyone in society can live with peace of mind
The government supports companies within a special economic zone by setting their taxes higher than elsewhere

answer.text: The government supports companies within a special economic zone by setting their taxes higher than elsewhere

questions.question: Compared to last year, this year's salary increased by 10%. During the same one year, prices also rose by 10% overall. How do you think this person's standard of living has changed compared to last year?

options.text: You can predict it became richer. Even if prices rose, if salary increases, life improves.
You can predict it became richer. Since salary increased, the money usable should have increased too.
You can predict it stayed the same. Because the salary increase and the price increase are the same.
You predict you can't judge. Salary and prices are separate matters and can't be compared.

answer.text: You can predict it stayed the same. Because the salary increase and the price increase are the same.

questions.question: Nominal wage rose 8%, and the inflation rate was 5%. At this time, what can be said happened to real wage?

options.text: Real wage rose. Because the rate of increase of nominal wage exceeds the inflation rate.
Real wage fell. Because inflation is occurring, it must necessarily fall.
Real wage is unchanged. Because salary and inflation rate are unrelated separate matters.
Real wage fell. Because the rate of increase of nominal wage is below the inflation rate.

answer.text: Real wage rose. Because the rate of increase of nominal wage exceeds the inflation rate.

questions.question: There's a person who has their own shop and bakes and sells bread themselves. Which does the income this person earns correspond to?

options.text: Labor income. Because they earn income in return for the work of baking bread every day.
Asset income. Because they hold the shop as an asset, and income is produced from it.
Labor income. Because baking bread at the shop is no different from being employed and working.
Business income. Because they run the shop themselves, and what's left after subtracting expenses from revenue becomes income.

answer.text: Business income. Because they run the shop themselves, and what's left after subtracting expenses from revenue becomes income.

questions.question: Which correctly explains remittance?

options.text: Money a company pays to an overseas business partner for product costs.
Money where part of labor income earned by working overseas is sent to family, becoming a pillar of the country's foreign currency income.
Money a person working overseas sends to family; since it's an individual matter, it's unrelated to the country's economy.
The domestic family that receives the remittance treats that amount as asset income.

answer.text: Money where part of labor income earned by working overseas is sent to family, becoming a pillar of the country's foreign currency income.

questions.question: A certain person's nominal wage is unchanged from last year. However, that person says, "Lately, life feels a little easier." If this statement is correct, which is the most conceivable reason?

options.text: Even if nominal wage is unchanged, increasing working hours naturally raises real wage.
If nominal wage is unchanged, real wage must also be unchanged, so this statement doesn't hold.
They started receiving remittances, which became the same as nominal wage substantially increasing.
Because prices fell, the amount buyable with the same nominal wage increased.

answer.text: Because prices fell, the amount buyable with the same nominal wage increased.

questions.question: Among the spending around you, which counts as a "fixed cost"?

options.text: The hamburger cost on a day out with friends
The monthly fee for a music streaming service
The lemonade cost bought at a stall for a change of pace
The cost of extra stationery bought before an exam

answer.text: The monthly fee for a music streaming service

questions.question:
There are the following four kinds of spending. Which combination gathers only the "things that change by month (variable costs)"?
① Rent
② Food costs
③ Monthly phone fee
④ Cost of buying clothes

options.text: ① and ②
① and ③
③ and ④
② and ④

answer.text: ② and ④

questions.question: Which is incorrect as an explanation of propensity to consume and propensity to save?

options.text: When income increases, propensity to consume and propensity to save both increase together.
Propensity to consume is the proportion of income put toward consumption, and that part is used for shopping and so on.
Propensity to save is the proportion of income put toward saving, and that part is kept for the future.
Propensity to consume and propensity to save have a relationship where if one increases, the other decreases.

answer.text: When income increases, propensity to consume and propensity to save both increase together.

questions.question: You have 500 EGP and are hesitating between putting it toward savings to buy something you want, or going to eat with friends on the weekend. When making a choice you're convinced about while conscious of opportunity cost, which is the most rational way to proceed?

options.text: A way of always choosing the cheaper option by calculating both amounts
A way of deciding which is the correct use and excluding the wrong one from the start
A way of comparing the two options and judging whether the one you give up is worth it
A way of choosing whichever you most strongly want right now and not thinking about the other

answer.text: A way of comparing the two options and judging whether the one you give up is worth it

questions.question: You're hesitating about whether to sign up next month for a monthly magazine service you can read leisurely at home. It's 150 EGP a month, deducted on a fixed schedule each month. When judging using the ideas of opportunity cost and fixed cost, which thinking gives the most sense of conviction?

options.text: A thinking of comparing what else you could do with 150 EGP each month against the high value of the magazine, and judging whether you can be convinced
A thinking of deciding not to sign up regardless of content, because you want to avoid increasing money that goes out on a fixed schedule
A thinking of signing up right away without minding other things, because the desire to read is strong now
A thinking that 150 EGP a month is cheap, so there's no need to hesitate and signing up for now is fine

answer.text: A thinking of comparing what else you could do with 150 EGP each month against the high value of the magazine, and judging whether you can be convinced

questions.question: What is disposable income?

options.text: Money where government subsidies are added to salary, becoming the total amount the household can use
Money left in the household's hands after rent and utility bills are subtracted from salary
Money left in the household's hands after food costs and medical costs are subtracted from salary
Money left in the household's hands after income tax and social insurance premiums are subtracted from salary

answer.text: Money left in the household's hands after income tax and social insurance premiums are subtracted from salary

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the phenomenon that the "paradox of thrift" shows?

options.text: A phenomenon where saving rational for the individual can cool the economy of society as a whole when everyone does it at the same time
An economic law where household saving and society's whole economy are inversely proportional, and the more saving increases the more the economy definitely cools
A phenomenon within a household where one household saving conversely makes that household's finances tighter
A phenomenon on the government's spending side where the government economizing its spending shrinks society's whole economy

answer.text: A phenomenon where saving rational for the individual can cool the economy of society as a whole when everyone does it at the same time

questions.question: Suppose your family's household finances became a little tight in a certain month. Based on what you've learned, which is the wisest judgment the household can take?

options.text: Refraining from saving itself, out of worry that your saving might cool society's whole economy
Reducing your household's spending in step with the movements of surrounding households
Distinguishing necessary spending and reviewable spending for the household, and reviewing within a reasonable range
Reviewing spending to suit your own convenience, since household management and society's economy are separate matters

answer.text: Distinguishing necessary spending and reviewable spending for the household, and reviewing within a reasonable range

questions.question: Which of the following best explains a government subsidy?

options.text: A mechanism where the government supports living costs only for specific households in difficulty. It uses taxes.
A mechanism where the government bears part of a product's price so the household burden can be reduced. It uses taxes.
A mechanism where the government gathers companies' corporate profit and distributes it to households. It uses money gathered from companies.
A mechanism where the government hands money directly to households to increase income. It uses money the government newly creates.

answer.text: A mechanism where the government bears part of a product's price so the household burden can be reduced. It uses taxes.

questions.question: At a certain time, the talk that "households are tight" spread across the whole country, and surrounding households are all strengthening saving at once. Your own household hasn't had that big a change. At this time, which of the following is the most appropriate policy for managing your own household?

options.text: Thinking it's fine to shop as much as you like, since your household's judgment is unconnected to society's whole economy
Judging that you don't need to think about household management at all, since the government gives subsidies and supports you
Reducing your household's spending uniformly and greatly, including necessary things, because those around you are saving
Distinguishing necessary spending and reviewable spending according to your own household's situation, judging while also being conscious of the connection with society as a whole

answer.text: Distinguishing necessary spending and reviewable spending according to your own household's situation, judging while also being conscious of the connection with society as a whole

questions.question: Which is a correct description of a budget?

options.text: Recording what you spent and how much on, after spending the money
Looking ahead at income and expenses and making a plan to avoid spending haphazardly
Making a plan to increase your working hours to raise your income itself
Making a plan to borrow from someone when you run short on money

answer.text: Looking ahead at income and expenses and making a plan to avoid spending haphazardly

questions.question: Which of the following is the most accurate statement about an income and expense tracker?

options.text: Whichever is larger, income or expenses, becomes the balance
The balance is set by income alone, and expenses have nothing to do with it
Income subtracted from expenses becomes the balance
Expenses subtracted from income becomes the balance

answer.text: Expenses subtracted from income becomes the balance

questions.question: One month, income was 600 EGP and expenses were 750 EGP. Which is a correct description of the situation?

options.text: The balance is minus 150 EGP—a deficit
The balance is 150 EGP—a surplus
Since there's 600 EGP of income, there's no problem
It's a state where the more you spend, the more money you have to use

answer.text: The balance is minus 150 EGP—a deficit

questions.question: When your monthly allowance is 1,000 EGP, how much can go to "wants" under the 50/30/20 rule?

options.text: 200 EGP
500 EGP
300 EGP
100 EGP

answer.text: 300 EGP

questions.question: Say your monthly allowance is 1,000 EGP. This month you spent 600 EGP on things like food and transportation, 250 EGP on eating out with friends, and kept the remaining 150 EGP in hand. Compared with the 50/30/20 rule, which of the following is the best judgment about this spending?

options.text: Spending on necessities is above the guide, so there's room to review
Spending on wants is above the guide, so there's room to review
The savings share meets the guide's 20%, so there's no problem
Since it stays within income, there's no need to mind the allocation

answer.text: Spending on necessities is above the guide, so there's room to review

lessons.unit: Personal Finance, Credit, and Decision Making

questions.question: This month you overspent and your allowance is running low. As you cut back further, which spending should you keep until last as a need (a necessity)?

options.text: Cafe money for going out when friends invite you
Money for a bag you newly wanted
Money to buy a just-released game
Transportation to get to school

answer.text: Transportation to get to school

questions.question: Your budget looks likely to go over this month. When you review and cut spending, what kind of spending is easiest to start with?

options.text: Review discretionary spending, which you can change by your own judgment, first
Cut the fixed costs that go out at a set amount each month first
Reduce essential spending, indispensable for living, first
Cut all spending uniformly by the same proportion

answer.text: Review discretionary spending, which you can change by your own judgment, first

questions.question:
Sort the following four expenses into "essential spending" and "discretionary spending." Which is the correctly sorted combination?
① Transportation to get to school
② Daily meals at home
③ Replacing a bag that still works
④ Cafe money for going out with friends

options.text: Essential = ①③ / Discretionary = ②④
Essential = ②④ / Discretionary = ①③
Essential = ①② / Discretionary = ③④
Essential = ③④ / Discretionary = ①②

answer.text: Essential = ①② / Discretionary = ③④

questions.question: You saw a "today-only limited sale" ad on social media and suddenly wanted the item. Which of the following is the best action to take?

options.text: Honor the fear of missing out that "today only" stirs up, and buy as fast as you can
Check how much you can use now, then judge in order whether it's necessary and whether it fits the budget
Figure it's fine as long as it fits the budget, and buy right away
Decide you can't tell the quality from an ad, and give up buying without checking

answer.text: Check how much you can use now, then judge in order whether it's necessary and whether it fits the budget

questions.question: You get 500 EGP as a monthly allowance. This month your budget looks likely to go over, and you want to review your spending. Which of the following is the best approach for the review?

options.text: Since essential spending must be secured, treat it as un-cuttable and limit the review to discretionary spending
Don't review what you're spending on—cover the shortfall using money meant for savings
Regret that this month's spending ran high, cut out discretionary spending, and tough it out
Review discretionary spending first, then check whether a want has slipped into essential spending too

answer.text: Review discretionary spending first, then check whether a want has slipped into essential spending too

lessons.unit: Personal Finance, Credit, and Decision Making

questions.question:
When you sort the following three goals into short-, mid-, and long-term, which is the correct combination?
① The cost of a school-commute bicycle you want to replace in 2 years
② The cost of studying abroad, which you want to attempt in 6 years
③ Startup funds for your own shop, which you want to open in 15 years

options.text: ① short-term ② mid-term ③ long-term
① mid-term ② long-term ③ short-term
① short-term ② long-term ③ mid-term
① long-term ② short-term ③ mid-term

answer.text: ① short-term ② mid-term ③ long-term

questions.question: Among the following scenes, which describes a "trade-off"?

options.text: The situation where you can choose only one—buying a game or setting money aside
The value of the money you couldn't set aside for a trip when you chose the game
Working out how much to set aside each month to reach a goal for a trip
Judging whether buying the game is a need or a want

answer.text: The situation where you can choose only one—buying a game or setting money aside

questions.question:
Among the following, which is the correct combination of situations for using the emergency fund (a sudden expense)?
① Treatment costs for a sudden illness
② A monthly school commuter pass
③ Repair costs for a bicycle that suddenly broke
④ The cost of a trip planned in advance

options.text: ② and ④
① and ④
① and ③
② and ③

answer.text: ① and ③

questions.question:
This month's savings slot is only 200 EGP. Among the following goals, which should you set aside for first, as the priority?
① The cost of a trip with friends you want to take in 1 year
② Travel costs for an overseas sports event you want to attend in 5 years
③ Startup preparation funds toward 10 years from now

options.text: Start with ③. The bigger the dream, like a startup, the sooner you should set aside for it
Start with ②. Five years leaves room, so it's easy to proceed methodically
Set aside evenly, 67 EGP to each of the three. They're all important
Start with ①. Its deadline is the nearest, so you need to set aside for it first, as the priority

answer.text: Start with ①. Its deadline is the nearest, so you need to set aside for it first, as the priority

questions.question: With a monthly savings slot of 200 EGP, you're thinking about how to use your savings. Among the following, which is the most balanced way of thinking?

options.text: Prioritize reaching goals early, and put the whole 200 EGP toward setting aside for goals
Build up the emergency fund and set aside for goals a little at a time, in parallel
Put the whole 200 EGP into the emergency fund, and set aside for goals next month
Since there are too many goals and it's hard to judge, watch how things go this month and do nothing

answer.text: Build up the emergency fund and set aside for goals a little at a time, in parallel

Personal Finance, Credit, and Decision Making

questions.question: Among the following, which best fits "goal funds"?

options.text: Money kept on hand to use right away for daily meals and transportation
Money you vaguely put in a money box, thinking it'd be nice to have for something
Money you set aside at a fixed amount each month for next year's family trip
Money kept ready to use right away in case you suddenly fall ill

answer.text: Money you set aside at a fixed amount each month for next year's family trip

questions.question: Among the following, which is fitting to keep as an "emergency fund"?

options.text: Money you set aside monthly for a family trip in six months
Money in your wallet for monthly food and transportation
Money you put in a money box because it was left over at month's end, with no set purpose
Money kept aside in case an appliance suddenly breaks and needs replacing

answer.text: Money kept aside in case an appliance suddenly breaks and needs replacing

questions.question:
Among ① to ⑤ below, which combination selects all that fit the "emergency fund" among the three purposes of savings?
① Money set aside at a fixed amount each month for next year's family trip
② Money kept ready to use right away for a sudden illness or injury
③ Money set aside little by little from a young age for life after stepping back from work
④ Money kept ready to use right away in case an appliance suddenly breaks
⑤ Money in your wallet for daily meals and transportation

options.text: ② only
② and ④ and ⑤
② and ④
① and ② and ④

answer.text: ② and ④

questions.question: Even when you mean to "save what's left over," why is it often hard to save? Which is the best-fitting reason?

options.text: Because when money stays on hand as spendable, you end up spending it, so even meaning to "save the rest," nothing's left
Because you lack the strong will to keep from spending, and with enough willpower you could leave a surplus and save
Because if you don't decide in advance what for and how much to save, the motivation to save doesn't last
Because people always spend every last bit of money on hand, so no matter the method, saving is hard

answer.text: Because when money stays on hand as spendable, you end up spending it, so even meaning to "save the rest," nothing's left

questions.question: A friend asks you for advice: "I mean to save, but I just can't. I'm also worried about emergencies, and I don't know where to start." Which of the following is the best advice?

options.text: First, start by holding back from buying what you want, with stronger resolve than before
Split savings by purpose, and start by setting aside the emergency fund for a rainy day first
To grow the money for a rainy day even a little, start by putting it all into investment
Without deciding a purpose, start by building the habit of putting whatever's left over into a money box each month

answer.text: Split savings by purpose, and start by setting aside the emergency fund for a rainy day first
