questions.question: Which of the following best describes "simple interest"?

options.text: Simple interest is a mechanism where a set interest rate is applied each year to the combined amount of principal and growth
Simple interest is a mechanism where the same interest rate is applied only to the principal each year, growing by the same amount
Simple interest is a mechanism where the interest rate on the principal itself changes a little each year as it grows
Simple interest is a mechanism where the principal and the growth each grow separately at the same interest rate

answer.text: Simple interest is a mechanism where the same interest rate is applied only to the principal each year, growing by the same amount

questions.question: Which of the following best describes "compound interest"?

options.text: A mechanism where interest applies only to the principal each year, and the amount it grows doesn't change year to year
A mechanism where the interest rate on the principal itself gets a little bigger each year as it grows
A mechanism where the growth from interest also joins the principal, and the same interest rate applies to that total each year
A mechanism where you add the same amount yourself each year to grow the total

answer.text: A mechanism where the growth from interest also joins the principal, and the same interest rate applies to that total each year

questions.question: Managing 1,000 EGP at 5% a year with compound interest gives about 1,629 EGP after 10 years and about 2,653 EGP after 20 years. Roughly how much did it grow in the first 10 years (0 to 10 years) and the next 10 years (10 to 20 years), and which is larger?

options.text: The first 10 years about 629 EGP, the next 10 years about 1,024 EGP; the next 10 years is larger
The first 10 years about 629 EGP, the next 10 years also about 629 EGP; both the same
The first 10 years about 1,024 EGP, the next 10 years about 629 EGP; the first 10 years is larger
The first 10 years about 500 EGP, the next 10 years also about 500 EGP; both the same

answer.text: The first 10 years about 629 EGP, the next 10 years about 1,024 EGP; the next 10 years is larger

questions.question: Say money grows 4% a year under some management method. Using the Rule of 72, roughly how many years until this money doubles?

options.text: About 4 years
About 72 years
About 36 years
About 18 years

answer.text: About 18 years

questions.question: Which of the following will result in the largest final amount when managed at 5% a year with compound interest?

options.text: Manage 1,000 EGP for 20 years with compound interest
Manage 2,000 EGP for 10 years with compound interest
Manage 1,000 EGP for 40 years with compound interest
Manage 3,000 EGP for 5 years with compound interest

answer.text: Manage 1,000 EGP for 40 years with compound interest

lessons.unit: Personal Finance, Credit, and Decision Making

questions.question: Which of the following counts as a "risk"?

options.text: The large repair cost when heavy rain damages your house's roof
The phone bill automatically debited at the same time each month
Meal money you set aside for a planned family meal out
Allowance you methodically set aside to buy a study guide

answer.text: The large repair cost when heavy rain damages your house's roof

questions.question: For "an emergency where you suddenly need a large sum—not striking everyone at once, but able to happen to anyone," which is the most rational way of thinking to prepare?

options.text: Each person saves a large sum, and when an emergency strikes, pays from their own savings
After an emergency strikes, borrow money each time from family or friends to pay
Many people put in a little money each, and whoever an emergency strikes receives from the pooled money
The state covers all the money for emergencies, so households prioritize food, utilities, and such

answer.text: Many people put in a little money each, and whoever an emergency strikes receives from the pooled money

questions.question: Among the following, which counts as public insurance (social insurance)?

options.text: Insurance deducted monthly from a company worker's salary, paying a benefit when they visit or stay in a hospital for illness or injury
Auto insurance where you choose the terms from an insurance company's products in case something happens to your car
Medical insurance you apply for yourself, comparing several insurance companies, to further lighten your out-of-pocket cost for a hospital stay
Fire insurance you contract with an insurance company for, in case your house is damaged by fire or disaster

answer.text: Insurance deducted monthly from a company worker's salary, paying a benefit when they visit or stay in a hospital for illness or injury

questions.question: Among the following combinations, which correctly sorts things into the three layers of preparing for risk—"self-help, mutual aid, and public help"?

options.text: Self-help: private auto insurance you enroll in yourself / Mutual aid: public medical insurance deducted from salary / Public help: an emergency fund saved in your own account
Self-help: an emergency fund saved in your own account / Mutual aid: private life insurance peers put in for / Public help: public medical insurance deducted from salary
Self-help: public medical insurance deducted from salary / Mutual aid: an emergency fund saved in your own account / Public help: private life insurance you choose to enroll in
Self-help: private life insurance peers put in for / Mutual aid: an emergency fund saved in your own account / Public help: auto insurance you enroll in yourself

answer.text: Self-help: an emergency fund saved in your own account / Mutual aid: private life insurance peers put in for / Public help: public medical insurance deducted from salary

questions.question: What is the key difference between Takaful and ordinary private insurance?

options.text: Takaful is run by the state with mandatory enrollment, while private insurance is enrolled in voluntarily—that's the difference
Takaful pays participants even without an emergency, while private insurance pays a benefit only in trouble—that's the difference
Takaful is run as everyone's common fund, while for private insurance the money collected becomes the company's profit—that's the difference
Both Takaful and private insurance are run by insurance companies for profit, with no difference in nature

answer.text: Takaful is run as everyone's common fund, while for private insurance the money collected becomes the company's profit—that's the difference

questions.question: When you have your own household in the future, what's the most rational way to prepare for small expenses that can happen fairly often (an appliance breaking, a sudden daily-goods replacement) and for large expenses that rarely happen but are big when they do (a long hospital stay for illness, major damage to your home)?

options.text: Use insurance for both small and large expenses. Sharing everything through mutual aid means you don't touch your own savings, so the burden is lightest
Use only your own savings for both small and large expenses. Preparing for everything with your own money avoids paying premiums, so it's the best deal long-term
Prepare for small expenses with insurance. Prepare for large expenses with your own savings. Covering frequently used things with insurance makes the monthly burden easier to predict
Prepare for small expenses with savings, and large expenses with insurance. Big risks like injury, accident, or disaster can be shared with many people to keep one person's burden down

answer.text: Prepare for small expenses with savings, and large expenses with insurance. Big risks like injury, accident, or disaster can be shared with many people to keep one person's burden down

questions.question: At an online shop, you selected an item and pressed "confirm order." After that, a reply "order confirmed" arrived from the store, you paid the price, and a few days later the item arrived. At which point was the contract formed?

options.text: When you pressed "confirm order"
When the store replied "order confirmed"
When you paid the store the price of the item
When the ordered item arrived in your hands

answer.text: When the store replied "order confirmed"

questions.question:
Which of the following is correct about the formation of a contract and contract documents?
① Even without a contract document, a contract forms if you promise each other out loud
② Even a light "sure" can be taken as acceptance
③ Unless you sign a contract document, you don't need to keep the promise
④ A contract document is made to lower the item's price

options.text: ① and ② and ③
② and ④
② and ③ and ④
① and ②

answer.text: ① and ②

questions.question: Among the following, which exchange counts as a legal "contract"?

options.text: Asking a clerk, "Is this item in stock?"
Promising a clerk, "I'll definitely come buy this tomorrow!"
Saying "this one, please" at the register, and the clerk responding "certainly"
Calling out to a clerk, "May I try on this outfit?"

answer.text: Saying "this one, please" at the register, and the clerk responding "certainly"

questions.question: A buyer who received goods at a store then goes without paying the price. Based on the rules of contracts, what happens next?

options.text: The moment the seller handed over the goods (fulfilled the obligation), all rights vanish, so the price can no longer be billed
The seller still has the right to receive the price (a claim), so the buyer can be billed for payment
If goods are handed over first, contractual rights vanish at that point, and the price can't be billed afterward
If the buyer doesn't fulfill the payment obligation, the contract automatically vanishes and the goods return to the store right away

answer.text: The seller still has the right to receive the price (a claim), so the buyer can be billed for payment

questions.question: You're looking at a pricey item you're unsure about buying at an online shop. Which of the following is the best way to think before confirming the order?

options.text: Since confirming forms a contract that's hard to cancel, decide after checking the cancellation rules on top of whether you need it, the price, and the contents
Since you can often easily cancel after confirming, first confirm and then think about whether to buy
Since a contract isn't formed until you pay, it's fine to think about whether to buy right up until just before payment
Since you can get it canceled by explaining your situation to the store even if you change your mind, just confirm the order first

answer.text: Since confirming forms a contract that's hard to cancel, decide after checking the cancellation rules on top of whether you need it, the price, and the contents

lessons.unit: Personal Finance, Credit, and Decision Making

questions.question: Picture yourself the moment you leave the store after shopping with a credit card. Which is the correct combination of the situation for the "item" and the "price" at this time?

options.text: [Item] not yet received / [Price] not yet paid
[Item] already received / [Price] not yet paid
[Item] not yet received / [Price] already paid
[Item] already received / [Price] already paid

answer.text: [Item] already received / [Price] not yet paid

questions.question: Shopping with a credit card is a promise by the consumer to "pay the money later." Even so, why doesn't the store have to worry "what if I don't get paid later"?

options.text: Because the store believes the consumer who'll pay later and waits for the payment
Because the consumer hands the store the price in cash when receiving the item
Because the credit company pays the store the price first, on the consumer's behalf
Because the store lends the consumer the money for the item on the spot

answer.text: Because the credit company pays the store the price first, on the consumer's behalf

questions.question: You couldn't gather the money to pay all at once, so you decided to buy with installment payment. To make the final total you pay (including the added-on amount) as small as possible, which payment way is good?

options.text: Make the monthly payment as large as you can within a range that doesn't strain your life, and pay over a short period
Make the monthly payment as small as possible and pay slowly over a long period
Since the length of the period doesn't relate to the total, pay with a focus on the smallness of the monthly payment
To finish even a day sooner, pay the maximum each month even by cutting into living expenses

answer.text: Make the monthly payment as large as you can within a range that doesn't strain your life, and pay over a short period

questions.question:
Among the following, which contains all the things that affect a credit score (raise or lower credit)?
① Continuing to make payments properly on the due dates
② The person's age or appearance
③ Failing to keep repayment promises, with payments repeatedly late
④ Finishing repaying borrowed money as planned

options.text: ① and ② and ③
① and ② and ④
② and ③ and ④
① and ③ and ④

answer.text: ① and ③ and ④

questions.question: When buying a computer with installment payment, which is the appropriate judgment?

options.text: Since you found you can pay the monthly amount on your current income, judge there'll be no problem in the future either
Since a contract can't easily be canceled partway, carefully consider whether you can keep paying to the end
If you can't pay partway, judge that you can just return the item and end the payments
Judge that revolving payment, which lowers the monthly amount further, lets you keep paying stably

answer.text: Since a contract can't easily be canceled partway, carefully consider whether you can keep paying to the end

questions.question: Suspicious stories have several features to watch for. Which of the following best matches a feature with how to deal with it?

options.text: Cautiously seeing "today-only discount sale" as a rushing tactic, cancel your store membership so as not to be deceived
Wary of "an official app's notification" as a fraud tactic to steal personal info, delete that app for safety
Wary of "an online-shop order confirmation email" as a fake bill, don't pay for goods you actually bought
Doubting an investment story of "you'll definitely make money" as a fraud feature, refuse firmly on the spot and consult a specialized helpline

answer.text: Doubting an investment story of "you'll definitely make money" as a fraud feature, refuse firmly on the spot and consult a specialized helpline

questions.question:
Which is a correct explanation about mechanisms that protect consumers?
① In some transactions, there can be a mechanism to cancel unconditionally within a set period even after contracting
② Since consumers are often at a disadvantage in information and bargaining power compared with businesses, there are mechanisms to protect them
③ When in trouble, you can consult a public consumer-protection helpline
④ Since there are mechanisms to protect consumers, there's no need to check the contents yourself when contracting

options.text: ① and ② and ③
① and ④
② and ③
② and ③ and ④

answer.text: ① and ② and ③

questions.question: You're unsure whether to borrow money and attend a school to earn a qualification useful for a future job. Which is the wisest way to think about dealing with "debt"?

options.text: If it's for the future, borrow right away and think about whether you can repay later
Since all debt is dangerous, never borrow for any reason whatsoever
After making a solid repayment plan, borrow as an investment in the future
Rather than borrow for a qualification, borrow to buy something you want now

answer.text: After making a solid repayment plan, borrow as an investment in the future

questions.question:
Which of the following is the correct combination of words for the blanks in the following sentence?
When a person struggling to repay repeatedly ( ① ) to repay, the debt swells and becomes unrepayable. This is called ( ② ).

options.text: ① extremely cuts living expenses / ② debt spiral
① borrows anew from somewhere else / ② debt spiral
① borrows anew from somewhere else / ② emergency fund
① has family front the money / ② default

answer.text: ① borrows anew from somewhere else / ② debt spiral

questions.question: You contracted to buy a suspicious product and are anxious that "it might have been a mistake." It's hard to consult even family, and you're wavering, thinking "I'll wait a few days and see," but which is the biggest reason you shouldn't put it off here?

options.text: Because once the actual product arrives home in a few days, returns become impossible even unopened
Because the more you delay paying, the more late fees are tacked on and the total to pay keeps growing
Because there's a mechanism with a set period for canceling the contract, and the more you wait, the more that deadline passes and it becomes unusable
Because the moment the other company contacts you to confirm, the contract becomes fully fixed and no changes are accepted after

answer.text: Because there's a mechanism with a set period for canceling the contract, and the more you wait, the more that deadline passes and it becomes unusable

questions.question: Among the following people, who can most be said to be "brimming with entrepreneurship," even without having started their own shop or company yet?

options.text: A clerk who focuses on handling document sorting and data entry at a company, perfectly following the set procedures and manual, accurately and without error every day

A shop clerk at the stationery store where they work, who noticed the register gets crowded at the start of a new term, planned a "new-term starter pack" bundling needed items themselves, and tried selling it

A company employee who observes in detail the methods of an already popular variety store, copies the same products with the same layout exactly, and is preparing to open a similar new shop themselves

A university student who studies daily in detail from books and seminars about company-registration procedures and how to write a business plan, hoping to start a business someday, but hasn't yet started moving

questions.question: Among the following business models, which best fits "social entrepreneurship," which aims to balance solving a social problem with economic activity?

options.text: Developing an application using innovative technology, raising funds from outside investors, and aiming for explosive market expansion and maximized company value in a short time
Continuing stable management over the long term within a reasonable range as a restaurant rooted in the local community, while prioritizing and protecting trust with existing customers
Quickly stocking short-term trend products in the market and flexibly switching handled goods to match demand swings, aiming to maximize immediate revenue and profit

Providing low-cost education services to people who lack learning opportunities like reading, writing, and arithmetic, securing business revenue to make the activity self-sustaining, while advancing the solution of the social problem of educational disparity

questions.question:

② At a restaurant with stores nationwide, keeping the set cooking procedures unchanged across all stores so that every store offers the same taste
③ Creating a new mechanism to deliver vegetables grown by neighborhood farmers directly from the grower to the home of the person who wants to buy, without going through a shop

options.text: ① and ②
① and ③
① and ④
① and ② and ③

questions.question: Which action best fits the "calculated risk-taking" that entrepreneurs value?

Believing only the gut feeling "this will definitely go viral!" and pouring all your funds at once into a new product
Calculating in advance the possibility of going into the red, making a plan to hold down losses, and taking on a new product
Aiming to grow the business scale big, increasing stores one after another on momentum alone without prior research

questions.question: A person often saw travelers struggling to carry big luggage up the stairs at stations and bus stops, and noticed, "it'd be nice if there were a new mechanism to carry this easily." Among the next moves to take, which best aligns with entrepreneurship?

Getting fired up with "I'll take on all the luggage in town at once," buying several high-performance, expensive carrier vehicles on loan from the start, and launching a large-scale paid service
Out of kindness, carrying luggage every time you see a troubled person, and continuing to help forever as "individual goodwill," within the range your own time allows
Making a proposal document saying "a mechanism like this would be convenient," and going to the government (city hall, etc.) counter to propose "please put out a budget and run it"

answer.text: Calling on a few people nearby, actually helping carry using carts and such, and testing small while confirming "what kind of help would really be appreciated"

questions.question: A person wants to start a service where neighbors can lend and borrow tools they don't usually use, via an app. Which expresses this wish as the strongest value proposition?

options.text: A service for everyone, where anyone from high schoolers to the elderly can casually borrow any tool, morning or night
An industry-latest service equipped with automatic matching by the newest AI, 24-hour phone support, and an insurance-backed compensation system
A service where people who don't want tools they use only a few times a year taking up storage space can borrow from nearby on their phone right away, without buying
A service that creates a big buzz before launch, with TV commercials featuring a popular celebrity and posters all over town

answer.text: A service where people who don't want tools they use only a few times a year taking up storage space can borrow from nearby on their phone right away, without buying

questions.question: A person thought of a new service idea. Before investing money and time in earnest, wanting to confirm whether there are really people who want it, they want to do market research. Which of the following is the most appropriate?

Making a survey on the internet that anyone can answer, having as many people as possible answer, and confirming by gathering the overall average opinion
Posting on your own social media "I'm thinking of starting a service like this," and confirming by the number of "likes" and comments that gather
Reading lots of news and word-of-mouth articles about similar existing services, and convincing yourself by analysis that there must be demand for your service too

answer.text: Meeting people who seem really troubled directly, and confirming in detail their past actual experiences and behavior—when they were last troubled, how they solve it now, and so on

questions.question: Among the following four, which effort best fits the MVP idea?

Someone who wants to sell phone cases online, rather than ordering a large amount at once, first handmakes just one, lists it on their online shop, and watches whether there are really people who buy
A person who wants to newly start a language class first has only family and close friends try it for free, and since it was well-received, opens the class in earnest as is
An app developer, thinking of a new app, puts out lots of large-scale ads before making it, gathers download reservations, and then starts development in earnest

answer.text: Someone who wants to sell phone cases online, rather than ordering a large amount at once, first handmakes just one, lists it on their online shop, and watches whether there are really people who buy

questions.question: When launching a new service, which order has the least risk and lets you proceed steadily?

options.text: Value proposition → notice the problem → market research → test small with an MVP
Notice the problem → market research → value proposition → test small with an MVP
Test small with an MVP → market research → value proposition → notice the problem
Notice the problem → value proposition → market research → test small with an MVP

questions.question: A person thought of a service connecting food a popular shop made that day and had left over, to young people who want to eat it at a bargain. Which of the following is the most appropriate way to confirm this as an MVP?

Yourself picking up leftover food from a nearby shop and distributing it to acquaintances every day, and watching their reactions
Connecting a few nearby shops and a few young people who want to eat, by just exchanging messages, and watching the reaction
Making a highly complete app, calling on the whole town's shops and young people, and testing in earnest to watch the reaction

questions.question:
Below, ① to ③ each fit which of the three risks of starting a business (funding, market, competition)? Choose the most appropriate combination from A to D.

① market, ② competition, ③ funding
① competition, ② market, ③ funding
① funding, ② competition, ③ market

questions.question: A person is trying to develop an original healthy juice and launch an online shop selling it. As "how to face risk" in starting a business, which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Until confident in the taste, testing it many times with just yourself and family, and putting it out after raising the completeness
First making just a small amount and selling a limited batch, watching the reactions of people who bought, and proceeding little by little
To not miss the chance by selling out, making a set amount in advance before confirming whether there are people who want it

answer.text: First making just a small amount and selling a limited batch, watching the reactions of people who bought, and proceeding little by little

questions.question: A certain town supports entrepreneurs' new challenges from the "ecosystem" viewpoint. About this town where the "ecosystem" is functioning, which is the correct explanation?

Only specific successful senior entrepreneurs carry the role of guiding all the juniors
Various people and organizations relate to each other, and there's an environment creating new value across the whole town
Abundant funds are provided, and the success of every person starting a business is completely guaranteed

questions.question: When a business gets on track, as the "social significance" it brings, which of the following is the most essential explanation?

Monopolizing the market and trying to keep as much profit as possible to your own company alone
Prioritizing profit above all, and proceeding without caring at all about the impact on the surroundings, like the burden on the environment
Completely letting go of profit and continuing as volunteering, with the result that the business itself can't keep going

questions.question: A person, to start a new business, was able to first test small with what they had on hand (a test sale) and gather the reactions (data) of people who bought. Posting the idea on social media, confirming whether many praising comments gather, and then proceeding next
Investigating in detail successful cases in the same industry, copying their way of proceeding, and proceeding next
Visiting regional seniors and government consultation counters, connecting to advice and the next support (funds, places)

answer.text: Visiting regional seniors and government consultation counters, connecting to advice and the next support (funds, places)

questions.question: You're about to start a business solving the trouble (need) of "wanting to shorten the time spent on daily cooking and make more room in my heart." To have as many people as possible use it, deliberately not narrowing the target, aiming to broadcast to all people
Consulting experts knowledgeable about cookware and cooking on "what kind of person to sell to," and taking in as many various wishes as possible
Investigating cooking goods trending online now, and, among people who seem to use them, choosing as the target the one thought to have the most fans

questions.question: A person starting a bike home-repair service is thinking this: "For people troubled by broken bikes, I want to fix the broken bike on the spot. What goodness (value) to deliver
Where and how to generate revenue
By what method to deliver the service to the other person

answer.text: Where and how to generate revenue

questions.question: A person runs a cafe selling delicious coffee. Even though many customers come every day, after paying material costs and rent, almost no profit stays in hand, and it's becoming hard to keep the shop going. Which of the following is the best idea to make the shop last?

options.text: To draw in more customers than now, putting up a big, prominent sign around town, or placing paid ads on social media
To beat other shops by making the coffee taste even better, newly stocking good-quality coffee beans and continuing to sell at the same price as before
Handmaking lots of original goods like T-shirts and mugs with the shop's logo, and starting to sell them in the store
Starting a plan where you can drink one coffee a day for a monthly fee, and a premium plan where paying an extra fee on the monthly fee adds a special menu

answer.text: Starting a plan where you can drink one coffee a day for a monthly fee, and a premium plan where paying an extra fee on the monthly fee adds a special menu

questions.question: A bento shop is trying to sell voluminous special bento, at an affordable price, at a store in an office district, to workers at a construction site in the suburbs. But checking against the four questions of a business model, there's a part that doesn't click. Which combination doesn't click?

options.text: Workers at a construction site in the suburbs and "voluminous special bento"
"Workers at a construction site in the suburbs" and "selling at a store in an office district"
"Voluminous special bento" and "an affordable price anyone can buy"
"Selling at a store in an office district" and "an affordable price anyone can buy"

answer.text: "Workers at a construction site in the suburbs" and "selling at a store in an office district"

questions.question: The following A to D are plans of four people who thought of new business ideas. Which one has the four questions of a business model (for whom, what, how to deliver, how to generate revenue) clicking together beautifully without contradiction?

options.text: For elderly people with weak teeth, developing a snack featuring a hard, crunchy texture and selling it in a shop. Besides single-item sales, also selling a 20-piece set slightly cheaper than buying singly.
For city-dwellers without a car, selling large closets. Having buyers come to the shop to see the actual item, and having them carry it home on foot themselves.
For busy people who can't take time for daily tidying, starting a home-visit service that cleans the house for them. Besides one-time use, preparing a "monthly regular plan" for repeat use.
For people seeking "a luxury for a special day once a year," selling super-luxurious high-end cakes. To have them buy casually, selling at a price cheaper than the market rate, at the shop counter.

answer.text: For busy people who can't take time for daily tidying, starting a home-visit service that cleans the house for them. Besides one-time use, preparing a "monthly regular plan" for repeat use.

questions.question: There's a bakery that bakes and sells bread, and a shoe-repair shop that fixes broken shoes. Which correctly divides these two into the one-time payment model and service type?

options.text: Bakery = one-time payment model, shoe-repair shop = service type
Bakery = service type, shoe-repair shop = one-time payment model
Both the bakery and the shoe-repair shop are one-time payment model, receiving payment for a thing
Both the bakery and the shoe-repair shop are service type, receiving payment for work

answer.text: Bakery = one-time payment model, shoe-repair shop = service type

questions.question:
Among the following, which count as the subscription model?
① A microwave you can use as your own, as much as you like, until it breaks
② A regular-delivery service where various breads arrive for a set monthly fee
③ Image-editing software you can use for one year by paying an annual usage fee
④ A moving service of carrying out luggage that you request when moving

options.text: ① and ②
① and ③
② and ④
② and ③

answer.text: ② and ③

questions.question: A certain phone app game can be played free by anyone. Even so, this company firmly generates money and keeps the business going long. As an explanation of "how it generates profit despite being free," which is NOT appropriate?

options.text: Basically anyone can play free, but it sells items that let you advance the game advantageously. Some people who want to reliably clear the game optionally use those items, generating profit
It's a free-to-play game, but the number of plays per day is limited. To play beyond the limit, you need to watch an ad video or use a paid item, generating profit there
Releasing the app completely free with no paid content, gathering a mass of "people who want to play without spending money." And spreading users by their word-of-mouth alone, generating profit
Precisely because it's free, being able to gather many people becomes a strength. Companies wanting to promote to them pay ad fees to display ad banners in the game, generating profit

answer.text: Releasing the app completely free with no paid content, gathering a mass of "people who want to play without spending money." And spreading users by their word-of-mouth alone, generating profit

questions.question: You're about to newly start a platform-model business. To make this business succeed, as an entrepreneur, which of the following is the most important viewpoint to be conscious of?

options.text: Since "buyers (people who want to buy)" will naturally gather later, first gather a mass of "sellers (shops)"
Gathering both "sellers" and "buyers" while keeping the numbers of both nicely balanced, so as not to lean to only one side
Developing cheap, delicious products yourselves, selling them directly to customers, and increasing fans of the service
Since users are few at first and profit is hard to make, setting the per-transaction brokerage fee as high as possible to secure revenue

answer.text: Gathering both "sellers" and "buyers" while keeping the numbers of both nicely balanced, so as not to lean to only one side

questions.question: A person thought, "I want to spread delicious ramen to the world." Among business models, as a feature when spreading shops with the "franchise model," which of the following is the most appropriate?

options.text: Not making ramen yourself, connecting "people who want to make ramen" and "people who want to eat ramen" via an app, and receiving that brokerage fee
Providing ramen to customers for "free" in exchange for receiving "ad fees" from companies that want to put up signs in the store, operating on that profit
The basic ramen is eatable by anyone for "free," but receiving payment "for a fee" only from some people who want toppings like char siu or soft-boiled egg
By borrowing the "sign" and "taste recipe" of an already-successful famous shop, being able to open shops in many places with lower failure risk, without training from scratch

answer.text: By borrowing the "sign" and "taste recipe" of an already-successful famous shop, being able to open shops in many places with lower failure risk, without training from scratch

questions.question: A certain internet service, rather than selling products itself, prepares "a place where people who want to sell and people who want to buy can meet." And each time a transaction between users is established, it receives part of that payment as income. What is this business's "mechanism for money coming in (revenue stream)"?

options.text: One-time payment model
Commission-based model
Recurring revenue model
Franchise model

answer.text: Commission-based model

questions.question: At a drink stall, because the material purchase price (raw material cost) rose, a price increase is being planned. When deciding the "price" to make the shop last, which of the following is the most important way of thinking?

options.text: Considering the possibility that customers decrease due to the price increase, examining the balance between price and "sellable quantity" and setting it
Adding the raised material cost directly onto the price, and further setting it high so the profit per cup is also more than before
Not caring how many customers decrease, setting it high so the profit left per cup sold is maximized
To absolutely not decrease customers, setting it even cheaper than before, even if the purchase price rose

answer.text: Considering the possibility that customers decrease due to the price increase, examining the balance between price and "sellable quantity" and setting it

questions.question: A small eatery wants to increase its LTV to keep the shop going long. Among the following, which is the most effective for raising LTV?

options.text: To draw in even one more new customer, handing out flyers or spending money on social media ads
To increase profit per visit, raising the food prices and switching to a menu using special high-end ingredients
To increase the whole shop's revenue, newly opening another same eatery in a different town, not just the current shop
To make customers who came once into fans, making a "point card" that becomes a discount coupon after 30 visits

answer.text: To make customers who came once into fans, making a "point card" that becomes a discount coupon after 30 visits

questions.question: At a company running a certain monthly internet service, despite working hard to acquire customers, the overall deficit keeps swelling, resulting in "unsustainable unit economics." At this time, which is the cause (situation) happening behind the scenes at the company?

options.text: The service became hugely popular, and ad costs came to be kept low. Furthermore, customers who became fans keep using it for years
CAC is unchanged. But due to word-of-mouth effect, customers have come to use the service longer than before
Competition with rival companies intensified, and CAC grew large. Furthermore, customers who got tired of the service came to cancel immediately
The way of placing internet ads improved, and customers came to be gathered cheaply. But the customers' service-use period is unchanged from before

answer.text: Competition with rival companies intensified, and CAC grew large. Furthermore, customers who got tired of the service came to cancel immediately

questions.question:
There are two businesses with different characteristics. Going forward, when you keep increasing customers, which business can grow sustainably and achieve a virtuous cycle of being in the black? Choose the one paired with the most appropriate reason.
[Business X] A mechanism easy to expand rapidly, but CAC stays above LTV.
[Business Y] The more customers increase, the more your own labor increases, but LTV firmly exceeds CAC.

options.text: Business X: because as long as there's an easy-to-expand mechanism, it grows naturally regardless of the cost balance per customer
Business Y: because the per-person economics work first, so the more customers increase, the more surely a rich cycle is born
Business X: because as long as there's a mechanism to gather many customers, it steadily goes into the black and the virtuous cycle continues
Business Y: because even if per customer is in the black, when customers increase labor increases too, so the more you increase, the more into the red

answer.text: Business Y: because the per-person economics work first, so the more customers increase, the more surely a rich cycle is born

questions.question:
Organizing the expenses for starting a food truck selling drinks. Among ① to ④ below, which of the following is the most appropriate combination of expenses that tend to cost more the more the number sold increases?
① A spot fee rented at 5,000 EGP a month
② Stocking cost for the fruit and tea leaves used in the drinks
③ Cost of the cups and straws the drinks go in
④ Wages to the people working

options.text: ① and ②
② and ③
③ and ④
① and ④

answer.text: ② and ③

questions.question:
A small sandwich shop is organizing the expenses that cost per month. Among ① to ④ below, which of the following is the most appropriate combination of fixed costs and variable costs?
① Money to rent the store for a set amount monthly
② Stocking cost for the bread and vegetables used in the sandwiches
③ Cost of the paper bags and wrapping paper used per order
④ Usage fee for using the register system monthly

options.text: Fixed = ①② / Variable = ③④
Fixed = ②④ / Variable = ①③
Fixed = ②③ / Variable = ①④
Fixed = ①④ / Variable = ②③

answer.text: Fixed = ①④ / Variable = ②③

questions.question: A small sandwich shop near a school decided to use slightly cheaper cheese than before, to hold down material costs. Given making expenses cheaper (cost-cutting) and the risk of the product's quality or customer satisfaction dropping (trade-off), as an entrepreneur, which of the following is the most appropriate action to think about together with "holding down expenses"?

options.text: Keeping all the money freed up by lowering material costs as profit in hand, to fill the shop's past deficit
Since materials got cheaper, lowering the sandwich price too, to the limit, and taking on rival shops with just "cheapness"
Covering the satisfaction that might drop from cheaper materials, with devices like adjusting the amount or look of the fillings, or more careful service
Accepting that regulars decreasing due to lower taste quality can't be helped, and using the freed-up expense on ads to gather new customers one after another

answer.text: Covering the satisfaction that might drop from cheaper materials, with devices like adjusting the amount or look of the fillings, or more careful service

questions.question: A certain shop has total fixed costs of 6,000 EGP every month to maintain the shop. Here, it decided to sell an item for 40 EGP each. This item costs 10 EGP in material cost (variable cost) per item. At the "break-even point," where the shop escapes the red and profit becomes exactly zero, how many items sold per month is it?

options.text: 150 items
600 items
200 items
120 items

answer.text: 200 items

questions.question: A certain shop's break-even point is 300 items a month. This month, this shop decided to sell more even by discounting, and managed to sell 320 items, but calculating, it went into the red. Which of the following is the most likely reason?

options.text: As a result of selling many beyond 300 items, the material cost (variable cost) per item automatically dropped, and revenue increased
Because, to have many people buy, it sold all products "discounted below usual"
As a result of selling many, the spot fee (fixed cost)—which should be a set monthly contract—rose just this month according to the number sold
Because there's a rule that as long as you exceed the 300-item goal, it automatically goes black no matter what price you sell at

answer.text: Because, to have many people buy, it sold all products "discounted below usual"

questions.question: A small sandwich shop is trying to find gross profit from the month's revenue. Among the following, which of the following is the most appropriate to subtract first when finding gross profit?

options.text: Tax charged later on the shop's profit
Stocking cost for the bread and vegetables used in the sandwiches
Money to rent the shop's spot, and money to helpers
Printing cost for flyers handed out to make the shop known

answer.text: Stocking cost for the bread and vegetables used in the sandwiches

questions.question: A certain small furniture manufacturing company's monthly figures are as follows. What is this company's operating profit? Revenue: 60,000 EGP; furniture material cost: 36,000 EGP; factory rent and labor cost: 15,000 EGP.

Which of the following correctly explains the types of costs subtracted from revenue and the resulting profit at each stage?
① Gross profit is revenue minus cost of goods sold
② Operating profit is gross profit minus SG&A
③ Net profit is operating profit minus tax and non-main-business flows
④ Net profit is revenue minus tax and non-main-business flows

options.text: ① and ②
② and ③ and ④
① and ③ and ④
① and ② and ③

answer.text: ① and ② and ③

questions.question:
For the following two shops, which is the correct way of comparing their final "net profit"?
Shop X: revenue 100,000 EGP, total monthly costs 96,000 EGP
Shop Y: revenue 40,000 EGP, total monthly costs 34,000 EGP

options.text: Since Shop X's revenue is large at 100,000 EGP, its net profit is also more than Shop Y
Even though Shop Y's revenue is small, its final net profit is more than Shop X
Since Shop X's revenue scale is large, plenty of net profit remains even after subtracting costs
Since Shop X has larger revenue, as a business it's more excellent and safer than Shop Y

answer.text: Even though Shop Y's revenue is small, its final net profit is more than Shop X

questions.question: A certain printing company delivered a large order and went black this month. However, the payment comes in next month. Meanwhile, for the next job, it needs to pay a lot of material costs in advance right now. At this time, which is the correct "way of seeing money"?

options.text: Calculating next month's incoming amount and the material costs needed right now, and thinking so as not to run out of cash on hand
Since profit is coming out, thinking next month's material costs can be paid with cash on hand no problem
Since the payment hasn't come in yet, thinking this shop went into the red
Thinking the payment coming next month is already money on hand, usable for other purchases

answer.text: Calculating next month's incoming amount and the material costs needed right now, and thinking so as not to run out of cash on hand

questions.question: If you use all of a personally-run shop's net profit for personal spending, such as living expenses, which of the following is the most likely negative consequence?

options.text: Turning net profit to personal spending, you become unable to pay the next month's material costs and such
The amount used is subtracted directly from revenue, and this month's net profit goes into the red
The portion for improving the shop, and the portion for preparing for sudden events, become unusable
By exactly the amount used for enjoyment, the next month's revenue necessarily decrease

answer.text: The portion for improving the shop, and the portion for preparing for sudden events, become unusable

questions.question:
A small company selling school supplies near a school divided a month's net profit into the following three. Which is the correct combination of these three uses?
① Keeping it within the company in preparation for expenses from sudden trouble or months when goods don't sell.
② Handing a portion of profit to the shareholders who put money into the company.
③ Bringing in new shelves and tools for managing the number of items, to make the shop easier to use.

options.text: ① dividends / ② retained earnings / ③ reinvestment
① retained earnings / ② dividends / ③ reinvestment
① reinvestment / ② dividends / ③ retained earnings
① retained earnings / ② reinvestment / ③ dividends

answer.text: ① retained earnings / ② dividends / ③ reinvestment

questions.question: There are two small printing shops that started from about the same profit. Shop X kept reinvesting a portion of its monthly net profit into equipment like new printers and computers. Meanwhile, Shop Y did no reinvestment at all and saved all its monthly net profit as is in hand. After a few years, as the change happening to the two shops, which of the following is the most appropriate?

options.text: Shop Y, having saved more money in hand, speeds up its work and becomes able to handle more customers
Shop X, having reduced its net profit by using it on other things, grows slower as a company than Shop Y, which didn't reinvest
Since both shops had the same starting net profit, no matter how they use the money, the company scale and net profit a few years later don't change
Shop X, thanks to new equipment, raises its work speed and quality, and as a result becomes more able to generate more net profit

answer.text: Shop X, thanks to new equipment, raises its work speed and quality, and as a result becomes more able to generate more net profit

questions.question: There's a small repair shop that just opened. This month a little profit came out, but the monthly order count is still unstable. Furthermore, the tools it uses are old, and a sudden replacement cost might arise soon. In this shop's "current situation," which of the following is the most appropriate use of net profit?

options.text: Securing cash that can withstand sudden expenses as a "reserve (stable management)," and considering tool improvement (reinvestment) within an affordable range
Thinking it a chance to make the shop famous all at once, not securing cash on hand, and pouring all net profit into advertising (reinvestment)
Since the shop's future is very uncertain, saving all net profit as cash and not using it on tool replacement or improvement (reinvestment)
To not lose to rival shops, using up all cash on hand and immediately introducing the latest large repair machine (reinvestment)

answer.text: Securing cash that can withstand sudden expenses as a "reserve (stable management)," and considering tool improvement (reinvestment) within an affordable range

questions.question:
Looking at the situations of the following two shops, which is the appropriate combination for using net profit?
Shop X: a small bakery near the station. Lately customers have increased, and popular products keep selling out by around noon. There's also a little room in cash on hand.
Shop Y: a small repair shop that just opened. The order count isn't stable yet, and the tools it uses are old, so a sudden replacement cost might become necessary.

options.text: Shop X secures more reserve, and Shop Y turns more to reinvestment into new machines
Both Shop X and Shop Y use all net profit on their own enjoyment
Shop X turns more to reinvestment into new equipment, and Shop Y secures more reserve
Both Shop X and Shop Y divide profit at the same ratio regardless of situation

answer.text: Shop X turns more to reinvestment into new equipment, and Shop Y secures more reserve

lessons.lesson: Entrepreneur SIM - From Idea to Business
Knowledge Check: Entrepreneur SIM - From Idea to Business

lessons.unit: Basics of Investing and Wealth Management

questions.question: In stock investment, it's said that a long "time (investment period)" of several years is needed to produce results. Which of the following best explains the reason for this?

options.text: Because the invested funds are kept in a safe place without being used anywhere, and the mechanism is that interest automatically accrues over time and it grows little by little

Because, regardless of the business content or growth of the investment target, you frequently repeat buying and selling, aiming only at price movements over a very short period of a few minutes to a few days
Because the invested money is ultimately used within society as operating funds for the company or business, and it takes time until the results of that growth (the return) come back
Because, whatever the target, the invested money is promised by the state or bank to grow "for certain" and "by a set amount" over time

answer.text: Because the invested money is ultimately used within society as operating funds for the company or business, and it takes time until the results of that growth (the return) come back

questions.question:
The following, X and Y, are each talking about how they use money toward a certain IT company. Are their actions and ways of thinking classified as "investment" or "speculation" in the stock market? Which of the following is the correct combination?
X: "Company P is apparently developing an innovative new product with an eye 20 years ahead. I'm expecting that future growth, and I want to support a business that enriches society, so I'll put out money long-term from now."
Y: "Company Q releases new software tomorrow. I'm not interested in the company's future or the software's content, but right after tomorrow's release it looks likely to rise for just an instant, so I'll buy today and sell right away tomorrow, aiming at profit from that difference."

options.text: X = investment / Y = speculation
X = speculation / Y = investment
X = investment / Y = investment
X = speculation / Y = speculation

answer.text: X = investment / Y = speculation

questions.question: Suppose "inflation" occurs in the world. At this time, which of the following is an appropriate description of the change in the value of the money we hold, or the response we should take?

options.text: When prices keep rising, the number of the deposit amount itself held in a bank account automatically decreases, and the assets on hand physically vanish
If you keep money in a bank, the number of the account amount doesn't change, so no matter how much prices rise, the quantity you can buy with that money (purchasing power) never decreases
Because the real value of money erodes due to rising prices, as the safest inflation measure, you should avoid investment and concentrate all your funds only in saving
Because the quantity you can buy with money (purchasing power) falls when prices rise, you adopt "investment," which grows assets in line with rising prices, as an effective preparation

answer.text: Because the quantity you can buy with money (purchasing power) falls when prices rise, you adopt "investment," which grows assets in line with rising prices, as an effective preparation

questions.question: A person is choosing where to place money they have no plans to use for the time being. This person wants to grow money patiently over a long time of about 10 years, and intends to accept the risk of the amount increasing or decreasing along the way. However, they don't want to rely on luck over a short period, like gambling. Which of the following best describes the way of dealing with money closest to this person's thinking, along with the most appropriate reason?

options.text: Saving: because if you store money in a safe place like a bank, the value of money doesn't fluctuate, and over the long period of 10 years, money grows a lot

Investment: because it's a method of investing in a company or business that seems likely to grow in the future, and though there's rise and fall in price along the way, you can raise it little by little over a long period
Speculation: because it's a method of repeating buying and selling aiming at price fluctuation over a short period, and it best suits this person's aim of "wanting to take a long time"

Investment: because it's a method of investing in a company or business likely to grow several years or more in the future, and once you start, there's no increase or decrease along the way and it doesn't depend on luck

answer.text: Investment: because it's a method of investing in a company or business that seems likely to grow in the future, and though there's rise and fall in price along the way, you can raise it little by little over a long period

questions.question:
A friend consults you about how to use money, as follows. Which of the following is the appropriate response you should take after hearing this?
"Even if I save in a bank, purchasing power falls due to inflation, so keeping it as cash is meaningless, right? So I intend to put all my money into a special method that can grow assets to double for certain in a short period."

options.text: Arguing that since the saved amount itself doesn't decrease from the account, there's no need to mind inflation risk, and persuading the friend to keep doing only bank deposits without any investment from now on

Since "speed" of investment is more important than anything for preventing the fall of purchasing power from inflation, recommending the friend execute that special method right now before prices rise further

While sympathizing with the sense of crisis about inflation, since no "certain in a short period" method exists in the world of investment, telling the friend about the dangers of scams and high-risk speculation, and dissuading them from putting in the full amount
Since surviving the uncertain era ahead requires the drive to take a chance without fearing risk, whatever the method, fully agreeing with and cheering on the big gamble the friend is about to make

answer.text: While sympathizing with the sense of crisis about inflation, since no "certain in a short period" method exists in the world of investment, telling the friend about the dangers of scams and high-risk speculation, and dissuading them from putting in the full amount

lessons.unit: Basics of Investing and Wealth Management

questions.question: A person looked into two investment targets. Investment target X was found to have a very small range of price movement, and investment target Y a very large range of price movement. Which of the following can be said about these two investment targets?

options.text: Because investment target X has a small range of price movement, its risk is small, but correspondingly its return tends to be large
Because investment target Y has a large range of price movement, its risk is large, but correspondingly its return tends to be small
Because investment target Y has a large range of price movement, its risk is large, but the return that comes back also tends to be large
Because investment target X has a small range of price movement, its risk is large, but the return that comes back also tends to be large

answer.text: Because investment target Y has a large range of price movement, its risk is large, but the return that comes back also tends to be large

questions.question: The "range of swing in return (risk)" accompanying investment has several kinds depending on its cause. Which of the following correctly pairs the four types of risk with their corresponding scenarios?

options.text: Credit risk: when you try to sell stock or an investment trust you hold and turn it into cash right away, no buyer is found in the market and you can't cash it right away
"Exchange rate risk": the value of an asset you hold in a foreign currency falls with the change in the exchange rate, and when you convert it to cash the amount decreases
"Market risk": the company you invested in falls into management trouble, and the interest or principal payment agreed in advance can no longer be continued
"Liquidity risk": due to a sharp fluctuation in the exchange rate, the amount, when converted, of an asset you hold in foreign money erodes

answer.text: "Exchange rate risk": the value of an asset you hold in a foreign currency falls with the change in the exchange rate, and when you convert it to cash the amount decreases

questions.question: A person is thinking of managing funds on hand, whose use is decided for three months later, only for that short period until then. When choosing an investment target, which of the following is an appropriate point this person should be especially careful about?

options.text: So they can reliably cash out at the needed timing, avoiding "liquidity risk"—that when they want to sell, a buyer isn't found right away
To grow the assets on hand to the maximum in the short period of three months, choosing an investment target with an expectation value of price rise as high as possible
Choosing a target that, even if the price temporarily falls, can be expected to rise if held patiently over several years
Since "exchange rate risk" can move both negatively and positively, devising to hold assets in foreign money as much as possible

answer.text: So they can reliably cash out at the needed timing, avoiding "liquidity risk"—that when they want to sell, a buyer isn't found right away

questions.question: When investing, the standard for how much "range of swing in return (risk)" you can accept is called "risk tolerance." Which of the following is the most appropriate way to decide your own risk tolerance?

options.text: Adopting, as your own standard as is, a "standard asset allocation for beginners" highly rated on the internet or social media
Based on the general guideline that "the younger the generation, the easier it is to recover over time even after failure," deciding mechanically in line with the standard for your age
Rather than your current situation, setting the standard based on how much return you want to receive, working backward from your future target amount
Judging based on your own concrete situation, such as "when you plan to use those funds" and "how much financial room you have"

answer.text: Judging based on your own concrete situation, such as "when you plan to use those funds" and "how much financial room you have"

questions.question: A person thinking of starting investment was searching for information online and saw several different ads. Based on what you've learned, which of the following is an inappropriate way to face this information?

options.text: A product written as "guarantees a fixed return every year": since the world of investment always has the risk that "invested money might grow or decrease," this product with the expression "guarantee" is better to doubt cautiously

A product written as "assets will double for certain!": generally, large return means large risk too, but the fact that someone actually wrote this sentence means there must be a way to grow money without risk

A product written as "for beginners, this is the only choice!": though written as for beginners, that's just how the writer perceives it, so it's important to properly confirm whether it suits your own risk tolerance and purpose

A product written as "exchange rate risk moves both up and down, so loss risk is zero": the possibility of moving both positively and negatively, and loss risk being zero, are completely separate matters, so doubt the basis of the explanation

answer.text: A product written as "assets will double for certain!": generally, large return means large risk too, but the fact that someone actually wrote this sentence means there must be a way to grow money without risk

lessons.unit: Basics of Investing and Wealth Management

questions.question: There's a person who doesn't need to grow assets a lot, so wants to manage funds while holding down the risk of price fluctuation (the range of price drop) as much as possible. Which of the following is the most appropriate combination of a suitable investment target for this person and its reason?

options.text: Stock: because if society as a whole or companies grow over the long-term from now, correspondingly the return obtainable in the future has the possibility of increasing greatly
Bond: because a company or country has the obligation to repay the principal, so compared to stock, the range of price fluctuation in the market (risk) is comparatively small
Stock: because even if the stock price temporarily falls, as long as the company produces profit you can receive dividends, so you can sufficiently make up for the loss from the price drop

Bond: because it's a certificate of lending money to a country or company, so regardless of the investee's management condition, when it matures the invested principal grows for certain and comes back

answer.text: Bond: because a company or country has the obligation to repay the principal, so compared to stock, the range of price fluctuation in the market (risk) is comparatively small

questions.question: There's a beginner with shallow investment knowledge and experience, holding unease about choosing investment targets alone. Which of the following is NOT good investment advice for this person?

options.text: Investment in "stock," whose price fluctuation is comparatively large, needs to be approached with a cautious attitude, especially until you get used to the market's waves
Even a "bond," whose price fluctuation is small compared to stock, should be recognized as not having completely zero risk of loss of principal
"Real estate," like land and buildings, always gathers buyers and can be cashed right away, so even a beginner with few funds can handle it easily
Using an "investment trust," where a specialist manages by dividing across multiple targets, lets you start from a comparatively low hurdle

answer.text: "Real estate," like land and buildings, always gathers buyers and can be cashed right away, so even a beginner with few funds can handle it easily

questions.question: There's a method of repeating, many times, the transaction of buying stock and selling it right away at the timing it rises within a few days. Which of the following is appropriate about the nature of this management?

options.text: It falls under "speculation" or "management close to speculation," aiming at short-term price fluctuation, and because it depends on immediate price prediction, the uncertainty (risk) of the management becomes extremely high

It falls under "speculation" or "management close to speculation," aiming at short-term price fluctuation, and by finely increasing the number of transactions, you can make market risk, like the waves of the economy, zero

It falls under "investment" or "management close to investment," aiming at mid-to-long-term growth, and because you can control the timing of buying and selling yourself, you can grow assets most efficiently

It falls under "investment" or "management close to investment," aiming at mid-to-long-term growth, and you can keep receiving dividends and gains on sale according to the company's growth over a long period

answer.text: It falls under "speculation" or "management close to speculation," aiming at short-term price fluctuation, and because it depends on immediate price prediction, the uncertainty (risk) of the management becomes extremely high

questions.question: Suppose a scene where you focus on gold as preparation for the risk that purchasing power falls due to inflation. Which of the following is an appropriate explanation of the management nature gold has?

options.text: Because it has a mechanism of interest and dividends, just by holding this asset, it can produce profit regularly and for certain
Because it's a strong asset unaffected by market price fluctuation, like economic crises, it can always be converted to cash at the same amount as when purchased
Because in scenes of rising prices, its value keeps rising worldwide in common, gold, with no risk of loss of principal at all, can be called the safest
Though it doesn't itself produce interest or dividends, because it holds its own unique value, it functions as a safe asset for when prices rise

answer.text: Though it doesn't itself produce interest or dividends, because it holds its own unique value, it functions as a safe asset for when prices rise

questions.question: Which of the following is an appropriate consideration when selecting an investment target?

options.text: To hold down future uncertainty to the extreme, prioritizing above all the selection of an investment target with the smallest risk (range of price fluctuation) and the maximum expected return
After grasping the three features an investment target has—risk, return, liquidity—choosing in line with your own objective risk tolerance (the nature and period of the funds)
Since the most important thing in asset management is the safety of the principal, judging based only on the smallness of risk, without considering the size of return or the ease of cashing out

Based on your own risk tolerance, if you want to maximize the growth efficiency of your total assets, emphasizing growth through long-term management and considering an investment target close to speculation

answer.text: After grasping the three features an investment target has—risk, return, liquidity—choosing in line with your own objective risk tolerance (the nature and period of the funds)

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the legal position and role of a person who bought stock and became a "shareholder"?

options.text: They directly own specific assets the company holds (land, buildings, etc.), and individually hold them divided up as their own property
They hold a "share (stock)," a part of the company's overall ownership subdivided, and as one of the company's owners are involved in the company's management and the results of its operation
They become a creditor who lent funds to the company, and take the position of demanding repayment of the principal by a predetermined due date
They register as a customer member supporting the company, solely for the purpose of enjoying periodically provided product benefits and service perks

answer.text: They hold a "share (stock)," a part of the company's overall ownership subdivided, and as one of the company's owners are involved in the company's management and the results of its operation

questions.question: Which of the following is the best example of a situation where a shareholder exercises their "voting rights"?

options.text: When reviewing a company's corporate-oriented services, comparing several plans and choosing the optimal contract plan for one's own company
Considering the timing of buying more or selling stock held, and deciding to hold off on additional investment this month based on the market trend
Discussing a company's new brand logo design within the shareholder community, and sending a volunteer opinion letter to management
Attending a company's general shareholders' meeting and casting a vote in favor of the agenda proposed by the board of directors, on the future business policy and executive appointments

answer.text: Attending a company's general shareholders' meeting and casting a vote in favor of the agenda proposed by the board of directors, on the future business policy and executive appointments

questions.question: A company produced a "net profit" after subtracting all costs, but that year it decided not to pay dividends to shareholders, and instead to use the funds for developing new products and renewing factory equipment. Which of the following best describes the nature of this decision and the impact it has afterward?

options.text: Since a company can freely choose whether to distribute profit as dividends or turn it to the next growth, it means a forward-looking investment with an eye on the company's future growth
Under society's laws and common rules, net profit is obligated to be entirely allocated to product development and equipment, so it's based on a compulsory disposal following the rules
Despite producing net profit, not paying dividends means failing to fulfill the obligation to pay shareholders, under laws or stock market rules

The decision not to pay dividends despite producing profit corresponds to a malicious act where management abandoned its responsibility to shareholders, since it doesn't distribute money to shareholders right away

answer.text: Since a company can freely choose whether to distribute profit as dividends or turn it to the next growth, it means a forward-looking investment with an eye on the company's future growth

questions.question: Which of the following is the best example of obtaining a capital gain in stock investment?

options.text: Holding stock in a food-and-drink company you support, and receiving 50 EGP in dividends regularly in your account as a distribution of the profit the company produced in its activities
Buying an apparel company's stock at 200 EGP per share, and since it became a hot topic online and the stock price rose to 500 EGP, continuing to carefully hold it in your account without selling
Buying a technology company's stock at 1,000 EGP per share, selling it all at the timing the stock price rose to 1,500 EGP, and locking in the difference of 500 EGP as your profit
As a perk (shareholder benefit) of holding stock in a company running a local cinema, getting 10% off each ticket price and watching movies more cheaply than usual

answer.text: Buying a technology company's stock at 1,000 EGP per share, selling it all at the timing the stock price rose to 1,500 EGP, and locking in the difference of 500 EGP as your profit

questions.question: Which of the following most accurately describes what it means to hold stock?

options.text: If you hold stock, you can reliably keep receiving both dividends (profit received while holding) and gains on price rise (profit coming out when sold) anytime, into the future, for certain

You become a position holding a part of the company (a joint owner), and take on, at your own responsibility, both the possibility of receiving profit when the company does well and the risk of loss when performance worsens
If you get a lot of stock, your voting rights at meetings grow too, so you can ignore other shareholders' opinions and freely decide the company's rules by yourself alone
Since the only purpose is supporting the company, even if the stock price falls and the money you invested decreases, that risk has nothing to do with you

answer.text: You become a position holding a part of the company (a joint owner), and take on, at your own responsibility, both the possibility of receiving profit when the company does well and the risk of loss when performance worsens
